domains.verdict_headline: The absence of a service layer is the right call and I would not add one — the officially maintained FastAPI full-stack template (last commit 2026-08-17) does exactly this, and this repo's `_owned.py`/`_enqueue.py` seams are better than that template. The two undocumented structural bets (tasks.py-as-service-layer, config god-object) are survivable at ≤100 users and get bounded answers; the real defects are three places where a rule the project already wrote down was applied in one layer and not the other — most seriously an import-time route branch that means the entire production SPA mount and its path-traversal guard are executed by zero tests in any CI lane.
strengths: No service layer is the correct call at this scale, and the targeted seams beat the reference: routers/_owned.py (47 lines) collapses fetch+ownership into one query returning 404 for both missing and foreign — the official FastAPI template writes that predicate inline in every handler; routers/_enqueue.py (75 lines) is the single enqueue+SSE-ownership seam behind 19 endpoints.

db.py:200 tenant_session(creator_id) takes the tenant id as a REQUIRED argument, so a call site structurally cannot forget the RLS GUC (55 uses in worker/tasks.py alone). This is better than what most funded teams ship.

39 of 40 Celery tasks pin name="worker.tasks.X" explicitly. Almost nobody does this before it bites them, and it is the single reason a tasks.py split is a 1-2 day job rather than a migration project.

clip_engine/ has real internal layering with a clean dependency direction — candidates -> sentence_snap -> merge -> scoring -> ranking -> render — with the impure surface concentrated in render.py/reframe.py and everything else pure and testable across 8,365 lines.

Structural tests are used as the architectural mechanism instead of layer boundaries: tests/test_worker_invariants.py pins the AdminSessionLocal allowlist, tests/test_usage_coverage.py pins that every LLM task bills, tests/test_model_config.py bans model literals, tests/test_ci_config.py gates the CI YAML. This fails loudly, which a layer boundary does not.

Incident-archaeology comments (worker/tasks.py:5334-5340, db.py:31-35, routers/thumbnails.py:167-177, main.py:188-210) name the incident behind each shape. Two of my findings were only findable because those comments documented the intended rule that the code elsewhere breaks.
unmade_decisions: 'We have no service layer, and here is why' — one paragraph stating that routers own their queries under _owned.py, that the domain packages ARE the layer, and that the official FastAPI template does the same. Marked reviewed-and-kept so the next session argues against a position rather than a vacuum.

The worker/tasks.py position: either 'one file, deliberately, until the envelope is extracted' or the concrete three-seam split (worker/sweeps/ ~1,480 lines / 14 beat tasks, worker/llm_features/ ~1,150 / 6 tasks, worker/render/ ~990 / 6 tasks, leaving ~2,900 in tasks.py). Either is defensible; the vacuum is not.

A task-body envelope contract: which session factory, when an advisory lock, when the spend guard, which progress events, which log_event. Currently re-derived across ~60 _async bodies. Same shape as the already-successful record_llm_usage choke point.

A rule for what belongs in Settings — proposal: only values that differ between local/staging/production; everything else is a module constant next to its algorithm. Would remove ~350 lines from config.py and a third of its 99-commit churn.

Test-registry policy: 'scan, don't list'. Any gate whose scope is a Python literal list (_LLM_MODULES, _LLM_CALL_SITE_FILES, run_layer0.py's _CANDIDATE_SOURCES, the hardcoded _TENANT_TABLES of OFF_COURSE_BUGS:25) is a vacuous-green generator by construction, and this repo has been bitten by that exact shape three times.

Where LLM calls are allowed to live. Issue 82b decided the session-order half but not the placement half. A one-line rule ('no LLM call in a request handler; use _enqueue.py') plus a ~10-line source-scan test over routers/ closes it permanently.

Which environments must register the full route table. Finding F1 exists because route registration is conditional on a build artifact and no gate notices. Either the SPA mount is always registered (serving a stub in dev) or one CI lane must build the bundle.

A deprecation policy for descoped artifacts — render.yaml (219 lines, and it encodes VERBOSE_LOGGING_ALLOW_PROD=true), deploy/charts/ (532 lines, never run), and the PgBouncer-shaped constants they justify in db.py:35,42 (prepare_threshold=None and pool_size=15 sized against a sidecar that is not in docker-compose.prod.yml).

findings.title: main.py registers the production SPA mount at import time, so no CI lane ever executes it (new instance of the repo's #1 failure mode)
findings.evidence: main.py:197 (_SPA_BUILT = _SPA_INDEX.is_file()), main.py:227-245 (conditional mount + /app/{spa_path} handler + traversal guard), tests/test_static.py:33,39,51,54,59,67 (skipif(not _SPA_BUILT)), frontend/playwright.config.ts:50 (webServer = npm run dev), .github/workflows/ci.yml:457 (only the non-required Frontend job builds the bundle), Dockerfile:71,95, .github/workflows/deploy.yml:122,136,345 (smoke = /health + llm_harness only)
findings.failure_scenario: Edit the traversal guard or spa_path fall-through in main.py's spa() handler. The pytest lanes have no frontend/dist so _SPA_BUILT is False and the routes are never registered — the four tests covering them self-skip; the required Playwright job talks to the Vite dev server, not FastAPI; the required Docker job builds but never runs the image. All 8 required checks go green. Production is the only environment where the branch is True, so the deploy ships and every signed-in creator's /app/dashboard 500s or serves the wrong bytes. Post-deploy smoke only probes /health, which passes, so deploy.yml's auto-rollback never fires. The path-traversal guard on user-controlled spa_path has zero automated coverage anywhere in the repo.
findings.standard: Route tables should not be conditionally registered on filesystem state at import time; the test environment must exercise the same route table as production. AUDIT_BRIEF §6 names this exact class ('an intermediate layer reports success without exercising the thing it claims to verify') and asks for instance #5.
findings.verifier_note: MEDIUM, not high. Accurate statement: the entire /app route table — the StaticFiles assets mount, the SPA shell fall-through, and the user-controlled `spa_path` path-traversal guard (main.py:227-243) — is registered only when frontend/dist/index.html exists at import time, and no required CI check ever exercises it: the pytest lanes have no bundle so all 6 covering tests self-skip (tests/test_static.py:54,64; tests/test_spa_serving.py x4), the Playwright gate runs against the Vite dev server with a mocked backend, and the Docker job builds the image without running it. The traversal guard has zero assertions repo-wide. Mitigations the finding omits: the maintainer's pre-push hook (scripts/ci_local.sh:114) does run these tests when a local dist is present, and deploy.yml's staging gate boots the real SPA-containing image and blocks on /health, so import-time/mount failures are caught. Residual real risk: handler-body regressions (fall-through, guard, content-type) reach prod with all 8 required checks green and post-deploy smoke passing. Fix is cheap and does not require restructuring the route table: monkeypatch-based coverage exists already at tests/test_static.py:44-51 for the `/` redirect; the same pattern plus a tmp-dir fixture bundle would cover the guard, or add one `/app/dashboard` + one `/app/../../etc/passwd` probe to the staging smoke.

findings.title: Two HTTP handlers hold a pooled DB connection across a multi-minute Anthropic call — the exact thing recorded decision Issue 82b forbids for routers
findings.evidence: routers/insights.py:824 (analyze_performer, session=Depends(get_session)), :764 (client timeout 120s, max_retries=2), :911 (await messages.create after 4 queries, transaction open); routers/thumbnails.py:182 (get_thumbnail_patterns), :273 (single-flight multimodal vision call over 10 images), knowledge/thumbnails.py:40; db.py:42-43 (pool_size=15, max_overflow=5), db.py:191 (get_session); docker-compose.prod.yml:14 (2 uvicorn workers); docs/DECISIONS.md:12284 ('82b router session-order: release before external call'), :12749; the correct pattern is documented in-repo at worker/tasks.py:5334-5340
findings.failure_scenario: Anthropic degrades with elevated latency (not errors; no circuit breaker exists). Each in-flight /insights/analyze-performer or /creators/me/thumbnail-patterns request pins one pooled connection in an open transaction for up to 360s (120s timeout x 3 attempts). ~7 creators retrying over a 6-minute window puts 20 such requests on one uvicorn worker, exhausting its 15+5 pool. Every other endpoint routed to that worker then blocks on pool_timeout and 500s. Cloudflare's /health check can still pass via the other worker, so an LLM slowdown becomes a half-traffic API outage with no alert.
findings.standard: Production LLM backends do not run inference inline in HTTP handlers — the pattern is POST -> 202 + job_id -> queue -> worker -> poll/SSE. Holding a DB session across a slow external call is a named FastAPI antipattern: release the connection before the external call and reacquire after. The repo already implements both rules elsewhere (routers/_enqueue.py behind 19 endpoints; worker/tasks.py:5334).
findings.verifier_note: MEDIUM, not high, and the finding should be scoped to the session-hold only. Accurate statement: routers/insights.py:824 (analyze_performer) and routers/thumbnails.py:182 (get_thumbnail_patterns) still hold a request-scoped AsyncSession in an open transaction across their Anthropic calls, contradicting the Issue 82b posture (DECISIONS.md:12284-12285) and contradicting DECISIONS.md:12749's claim that the last three such holds were closed — so the residual is a doc-accuracy defect as much as a code one. The fix is the documented in-repo pattern, not a rearchitecture: read -> release/close the session -> await the LLM -> reacquire a re-stamped tenant session for the write (worker/tasks.py ledger_session_factory precedent; chat.runner's session_factory signature). Drop the 'must become POST -> 202 + job_id' prescription: analyze_performer is a 256-max-token Haiku call and inline is a reasonable choice; the sibling start_thumbnail_concepts already uses 202 for the genuinely long work. Blast radius at <=100 users on 2 uvicorn workers with 20/hour + 10/hour per-creator caps, a 24h cache and a single-flight lock is small; file it as a hardening item, not an incident risk.

findings.title: worker/tasks.py at 7,179 lines: split three seams if you want, but the envelope duplication — not the line count — is what actually caused the defects
findings.evidence: worker/tasks.py (7,179 lines, 40 @celery.task decorators, ~60 _async bodies, 241 function-local imports); 39/40 tasks pin name="worker.tasks.X" explicitly — the exception is distill_style_prefs at worker/tasks.py:1574 (enqueued from routers/video_review.py:125); worker/celery_app.py:84 and worker/schedule.py address tasks by string name; 280 worker.tasks.<symbol> patch targets across 85 test files (60 distinct symbols); envelope repetition inside the file: tenant_session 55x, AdminSessionLocal 47x, progress.aemit 116x, log_event 38x, _try_advisory_lock 18x, _spend_guard_blocked 10x; sample envelope-heavy body at worker/tasks.py:5319-5400
findings.failure_scenario: Not a runtime failure — a recurrence mechanism. Every logged defect in this file (OFF_COURSE_BUGS :56 format drift, :98 mislabeled log fields, :61 advisory-lock leak, unbilled LLM calls, open redelivery double-spend) is a cross-cutting concern omitted from one hand-rolled task body, not a size defect. A four-way file split leaves all five classes exactly as likely: the next task author still re-derives which session factory to use, whether to take a lock, and whether to check the spend guard, with nothing enforcing the answer. Separately, splitting before adding name= to distill_style_prefs would change its auto-derived task name and orphan in-flight Redis messages.
findings.standard: Celery's own guidance prescribes a tasks/ package with explicit name= per task and gives no size threshold — the naming discipline is the load-bearing part, and it is already done here. Community FastAPI structure guidance (zhanymkanov) prescribes domain packages, which this repo already has. The 2025-26 YAGNI counter-literature warns against adding a layer with one implementation.

findings.title: The LLM conformance gate is a hand-maintained literal list, and preference/style_distill.py already slipped past it with no timeout and no max_retries
findings.evidence: tests/test_llm_conformance.py:34-47 (_LLM_MODULES, 13 literal paths) and :240-247 (_LLM_CALL_SITE_FILES, 6 literal paths); preference/style_distill.py:31 — AsyncAnthropic(api_key=...) with no timeout/max_retries; also absent from both lists: analysis/video_context.py:55, knowledge/clip_metadata.py:47, routers/insights.py:764, routers/thumbnails.py; anthropic==0.105.2 default is Timeout(connect=5.0, read=600, write=600); config.py:753 CELERY_SOFT_TIME_LIMIT_S=3000; docker-compose.prod.yml:46 --concurrency=4
findings.failure_scenario: Anthropic hangs a style-distill request. distill_style_prefs (worker/tasks.py:1574, enqueued from routers/review.py:319 on creator review feedback) blocks 600s and retries twice — ~30 minutes on one worker slot, comfortably inside the 3000s soft time limit so nothing kills it. Four creators leaving feedback during the same incident consume all four default-queue slots: ingest, transcribe, generate-clips, DNA build, chat and every beat sweep stop dispatching for half an hour, with no error and no alert. The observable symptom is 'uploads are stuck' and the cause is a missing keyword argument in an unrelated module.
findings.standard: Structural gates should discover their targets by scanning source, not by enumerating them in a literal — an opt-in registry is a vacuous-green generator by construction. This repo already does discovery correctly in frontend/src/test/sourceScan.ts and tests/test_model_config.py. Every external SDK client needs an explicit timeout well below the task time limit (the repo's own Issue 37 rule).

findings.title: clip_engine.edits.clip_origin_s was extracted as 'the ONE origin rule' (Issue 475) but is imported at 1 of 14 call sites
findings.evidence: clip_engine/edits.py:360-371 (docstring: 'The ONE origin rule (Issue 475) ... so no surface can mis-measure clips'); docs/DECISIONS.md:13014 records adoption by lift + originality fingerprint only; sole importer routers/insights.py:29; inline reimplementations at routers/clips.py:546,1168,1563,2276,2388,2495,2725; worker/tasks.py:783,2457,2556,2657,2867; chat/tools.py:498. worker/tasks.py:2448-2457 is a named byte-for-byte duplicate (_render_start_for) with its own docstring.
findings.failure_scenario: The rule is one clamp away from non-trivial — e.g. adding max(0.0, ...) for clips whose setup lead runs before t=0, or accounting for a leading trim in the edit document. The author edits clip_engine/edits.py because it is the documented single source and the docstring says so. The rendered bytes (worker/tasks.py:2457) and the clip-relative transcript/trim windows served to the editor (routers/clips.py:1168, 1563) keep the old semantics, so the waveform, the trim handles and the delivered video disagree about second 0 — exactly the class Issue 475 was filed to close. tests/eval/scenarios/*.yaml cannot see it: they assert candidate geometry, not render origin.
findings.standard: DRY on load-bearing domain rules, enforced structurally rather than by convention. The repo's own house pattern for exactly this is a source-scanning test (frontend/src/test/sourceScan.ts ships four of them); none exists for the origin rule.

findings.title: 67 clip-engine algorithm constants are env-settable Settings fields that no deployment sets, on a class with extra='ignore'
findings.evidence: config.py:35 (SettingsConfigDict(env_file='.env', extra='ignore')); config.py:311-660 = 67 settings across 12 clip-engine sections; 66 of the 67 documented in .env.example; measured: 0 of the 67 are set in docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.prod.yml, docker-compose.staging.yml, render.yaml or .github/workflows/deploy.yml; config.py has 99 commits (#2 most-churned code file); deploy.yml:180-182 explicitly excludes VM-managed secrets from the sync
findings.failure_scenario: An operator hand-edits /opt/autoclip/.env (which deploy.yml does not sync) to tune a reframe or overlay-band constant and misspells the key, or the key was renamed in a later release. extra='ignore' drops it silently — no error, no log line — and the algorithm runs on its default while the operator believes it is tuned. The repo has already been bitten three times by the same silent-unset shape: STORAGE_BACKEND left at local (uploads silently failed), BACKUP_R2_BUCKET never set (every prod migration ran with no safety dump), METRICS_TOKEN never set (/metrics disabled in prod). There is still no .env.example<->config.py parity test.
findings.standard: 12-Factor III: config is what varies between deploys, and explicitly excludes internal application config, which belongs in code. pydantic-settings docs recommend nested BaseModel groups with env_nested_delimiter for large settings sets — but that migration renames all 214 env vars, whose failure mode is precisely this project's worst defect class. The correct move here is deletion from Settings, not nesting.
findings.verifier_note: Keep at LOW, and narrow it. Accurate statement: config.py:311-660 defines 67 clip-engine Settings fields, none of which is set by any committed deployment config (all five checked), and 66 of which are documented in .env.example. Roughly 55 of those are genuine internal algorithm constants that 12-Factor III would place in code — but ~8 are legitimate deploy-varying items (seven feature toggles plus MEDIAPIPE_FACE_MODEL_PATH) and several others are documented, deliberate pre-calibration tunables (DECISIONS.md:906 on REFRAME_MIN_MAPPING_CONFIDENCE; the 'UNVALIDATED starting point' comments in config.py), so 'delete them from Settings' is the wrong blanket recommendation. Drop the extra='ignore' failure scenario entirely: extra='forbid' is not an option (six .env.example keys are consumed outside Settings), and none of the three cited precedent incidents were caused by a silently-ignored key — all three were never-set variables. The real, cheap residual worth filing is the one the finding proves and then buries: there is no .env.example<->config.py parity test (only tests/test_beat_ha.py:111's single hardcoded check), and eight Settings fields are currently undocumented in .env.example — ANTHROPIC_MODEL_CLIP_CAPTIONS, ANTHROPIC_MODEL_CLIP_EXPLAIN, ANTHROPIC_MODEL_CLIP_TITLES, CELERY_SOFT_TIME_LIMIT_S, COST_CACHE_WRITE_MULTIPLIER, MAX_INGESTED_CHANNEL_TITLE_CHARS, REDBEAT_REDIS_URL, YOUTUBE_PUBLISH_PRIVACY.

domains.verdict_headline: Migration discipline here is top-decile — self-documenting, offline-mode-aware, expand-only migrations with correct enum and deferred-constraint handling, and RLS as a structural property rather than a convention. The weakness is the boundary between models and database: 20 of 28 production indexes are invisible to Base.metadata and no `alembic check` gate exists, so nothing in CI notices divergence. Two live instances of the project's own #1 failure class sit in this domain: a pgvector HNSW index (with a green integration test attesting to it) serving a query that exists nowhere in the codebase, and a `clip_impressions` table written on every clip-list GET that no production code reads.
strengths: Migrations are top-decile. 0059_clip_blended_score.py documents why there is deliberately no backfill (the blend cannot be un-mixed), why no new RLS policy (RLS is table-scoped), why no index, and which template it follows. 0062_delete_masking_skip_feedback.py is a batched, idempotent, offline-mode-aware data repair with a termination proof in a comment and an audit log line that explains why it is WARNING not INFO (alembic's NullHandler swallows INFO).

alembic/env.py:47-58 carries the full incident archaeology for why lock_timeout/statement_timeout must go through libpq `options` rather than a pre-transaction SET — the root cause of the silent-no-op-migration outage — and the fix is structural at the site of the mistake.

Postgres enum discipline is correct, which is rare: 0032_clip_publication_schedule.py:49-54 uses ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS outside a transaction with the constraint noted, and 0057 chose a CHECK constraint over an enum precisely because ADD VALUE cannot run in one. 22 sa.Enum columns, no drift.

Clip.__table_args__ (models.py:730-745): a DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED UNIQUE(video_id, rank) with a comment explaining that immediate checking would fire on rerank_with_preference's transient rank permutation — a correct and non-obvious use of deferred constraints.

Clip.triage's server_default is load-bearing and says so (models.py:827-836): without a database-side default, the previous image's INSERT during a rolling restart would violate NOT NULL and 500 clip generation for the whole window. The expand/contract invariant applied correctly at column level.

RLS is a structural property, not a convention: 27 tenant_isolation policies, FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, the NULLIF hardening in 0045, db.py::tenant_session taking creator_id as a required argument so a call site cannot forget it, and clip_edit_documents denormalising creator_id so the policy is a direct-column comparison — a named house pattern. Above current standard.
unmade_decisions: Index ownership + a schema-drift gate: 'every DB index is declared in __table_args__; `alembic check` is a required CI job', plus the one-time migration that makes it true. Highest-leverage item in the domain.

JSONB payload versioning policy: a version bump requires either a read-time upcaster or a backfill migration, never a silent fallback — and one house rule for reject-vs-degrade on mismatch (the repo currently does both).
When a JSONB key graduates to a column. 36 JSONB columns, no stated trigger. The 2026 answer is 'when it is filtered on, or updated independently of the rest of the document'.

That `clips` stays one table across engine/verdict/render/delivery lifecycles, with column projection on read paths as the cost control rather than normalisation — recorded so the next refactor argues against a position instead of a vacuum.

A read-path column-projection rule: no ORM full-entity select() on a list endpoint for a table carrying a >2 KiB JSONB column. Gate-able as a source-scanning test, which this repo already does well on the frontend (src/test/sourceScan.ts).
clip_impressions: add (creator_id, shown_at) + a 90-day purge matching the event_logs precedent the decision itself invoked, or drop the table until its consumer exists.
pgvector: replace Issue 56's 'revisit at scale' deferral with 'no ANN index until an ANN query exists; when one is written, hnsw.iterative_scan is mandatory' — and drop ix_dna_embeddings_hnsw now.
docs/COMPLIANCE.md rows for dna_embeddings plus the eight other absent tables, and a storage-cost position for the 'until account deletion' classes (Issue 293 has no position).

findings.title: pgvector HNSW index (and its green integration test) serves a `<=>` query that does not exist anywhere in the codebase
findings.evidence: alembic/versions/0006_vector_and_fk_indexes.py:40-42; tests/test_vector_index_integration.py:35-39; routers/insights.py:666-671; knowledge/originality.py; dna/embeddings.py:101,137,195; docs/DECISIONS.md:9535-9539
findings.failure_scenario: A repo-wide grep for every pgvector operator/helper (`<=>`, `<->`, `<#>`, cosine_distance, l2_distance, max_inner_product) over non-test, non-alembic Python returns zero hits; the only `<=>` in the tree is tests/test_db.py:57, a `WHERE id = :id` point lookup that cannot use an HNSW index. The only production reader of dna_embeddings selects by exact predicate and computes cosine in Python. Consequence: every embed_clip_excerpts/embed_patterns/embed_brief insert pays an HNSW graph insertion at ef_construction=200 (~200 distance computations over 4KB float4 vectors, plus index pages and WAL) on the same VM running ffmpeg/MediaPipe, forever, for zero read benefit — while an integration test reports GREEN on infrastructure with no consumer. It also moots Issue 56's deferral: 'RLS is evaluated post-index-scan so cross-tenant embeddings appear in ANN candidates' cannot fire at any scale because there is no ANN scan. The recorded position is also mis-stated — the real hazard of post-index-scan filtering is not exposure (LIMIT applies after the RLS qual) but silent recall collapse (asking for 10, getting 1).
findings.standard: pgvector 0.8.0 (Oct 2024) added iterative index scans (`hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order|relaxed_order`, bounded by `hnsw.max_scan_tuples`=20000) precisely because HNSW returns a fixed candidate batch (`hnsw.ef_search` default 40) that a selective filter can decimate — pgvector's own docs cite '10% selectivity → 4 rows on average'. For a tenant-filtered corpus of thousands of vectors the 2026 default advice is simpler: do not use an ANN index at all; exact scan is faster and exact below ~1e4–1e5 vectors.
findings.verifier_note: Severity: LOW (not medium). Accurate statement: ix_dna_embeddings_hnsw has no reader and never has had one - git history confirms no production pgvector distance operator has ever existed in this repo, so docs/DECISIONS.md:8957-8967's justification ('the `<=>` cosine query was an unindexed O(rows) scan') is false; the only `<=>` in the tree is a PK point lookup in tests/test_db.py:57. tests/test_vector_index_integration.py is therefore a green test over unconsumed infrastructure, and that (not performance) is where its value lies. The insert-time cost is real but negligible at beta scale; do not justify action on performance grounds. The related observation that Issue 56's 'RLS is evaluated post-index-scan so cross-tenant embeddings appear in ANN candidates' tradeoff (DECISIONS.md:9554-9558) is unfalsifiable because no ANN scan exists is correct, as is the point that the real hazard of post-index-scan filtering is recall collapse rather than exposure. Recommended action is documentation/test honesty (drop the index and its test, or state it is pre-provisioned for a future ANN reader), not a performance fix.

findings.title: `list_clips` selects a ~15–20 KB TOASTed JSONB column for up to 100 rows to compute one boolean
findings.evidence: routers/clips.py:824-830 (`select(Clip)`, no load_only/defer); routers/clips.py:334 (`"has_crop_track": clip.reframe_track_jsonb is not None`); models.py:862-870; clip_engine/reframe.py:1034-1075; config.py:374 (REFRAME_SAMPLE_FPS=5.0); dna/builder.py:153-156
findings.failure_scenario: A creator opens the Review page for a video with 12 auto-rendered clips. Postgres detoasts and ships ~180 KB of JSONB (≈1.5–2 MB at the 100-clip cap), psycopg parses it all into Python dicts and SQLAlchemy hydrates ORM instances — every byte discarded after an `is not None`. models.py:862-870 states the intent explicitly ('the list surface only carries the boolean has_crop_track (a track is ~15–20 KB)') and the query defeats it. Same class twice more: clips.signals_jsonb is loaded whole to read two string keys, and dna/builder.py::_load_hook_texts loads every Transcript entity in full (segments_jsonb is the largest payload in the system) to extract one opening sentence per video.
findings.standard: JSONB query performance degrades 2–10× once a value exceeds ~2 KiB because the datum is TOASTed out of line; the actionable rule is 'select hundreds of rows but NOT the very large column'. Detoast is not even shared within a single query. Fix is column projection (`load_only` + a projected `IS NOT NULL` expression), not a schema change.
findings.verifier_note: Severity: LOW (not medium). Accurate scope: two instances, not three. (a) routers/clips.py:824-830 loads reframe_track_jsonb for up to 100 rows to compute one boolean, contradicting the stated design in models.py:862-870 - real, fixed by load_only plus a projected `reframe_track_jsonb IS NOT NULL` expression, but worth only a few ms at realistic clip counts and only for clips rendered since the 2026-08-05 flag flip. (b) dna/builder.py:153-156 `select(Transcript)` hydrates full word-level segments_jsonb per video to extract ~20 words - the bigger payload, but on a worker path. DROP the signals_jsonb instance entirely: those keys are returned to the client in _clip_response, and the column is small enough that it typically will not be TOASTed at all.

findings.title: 20 of 28 production indexes are absent from Base.metadata and no CI job compares models to schema
findings.evidence: alembic/env.py:18 (`target_metadata = Base.metadata`, no include_object filter); 28 named indexes across alembic/versions/*.py vs 17 index sites in models.py (verified by diffing Base.metadata under .venv/bin/python); .github/workflows/ci.yml:255-300 (migration-lint is path-filtered on alembic/versions/ and non-required per docs/BRANCHING.md:100-127); no `alembic check` anywhere in .github/, scripts/, tests/
findings.failure_scenario: A: a session runs `alembic revision --autogenerate -m "add X"`. Alembic emits op.add_column plus 20 op.drop_index operations (including ix_clips_video_id, ix_clips_creator_id, ix_videos_creator_id, ix_dna_embeddings_hnsw). migration-lint is advisory and its downgrade round-trip passes a deliberate drop cleanly, so `list_clips`' WHERE video_id becomes a seq scan and DELETE FROM creators seq-scans every child table. B (more likely): a column is added to models.py with no migration. migration-lint is skipped (paths-filter), the unit lane mocks the DB at the session boundary, and the 191 integration tests may not touch that column — so CI is green. In production `alembic upgrade head` is a legitimate no-op, the image swaps, and every request on that model returns 500 `column clips.foo does not exist`. The existing `alembic current == head` deploy assertion cannot catch this, because head genuinely is head.
findings.standard: `alembic check` (Alembic ≥1.9; this repo pins 1.14.0) runs the autogenerate comparison and exits non-zero if any operation would be rendered — the settled 2026 CI gate for schema drift, adopted by projects as large as Airflow. The standard is not 'indexes must live in models.py' but 'whatever the DB has, Base.metadata must also have, and CI must prove it'. It would fail today, which is the point.

findings.title: `clip_impressions` is written (and committed) on every clip-list GET and read by no production code
findings.evidence: routers/clips.py:857-877 (insert + commit inside a GET); models.py:1092-1104 (no index of any kind beyond PK); no ClipImpression/clip_impressions reference outside models.py, routers/clips.py and tests/; worker/tasks.py:1273,1318,1373 (the only three purge beat tasks — none touches this table); docs/DECISIONS.md:2252-2260
findings.failure_scenario: The write rate is keyed to page views, not clips produced — one row per ranked clip per list_clips call — so a 100-user beta reaches millions of rows/year, each costing a COMMIT on a read path (list_clips can therefore never be served by a read replica, and the request session is committed mid-handler). Eighteen months in, someone writes the IPS harness the table exists for; the first query `WHERE creator_id = ? AND shown_at > ?` over a multi-million-row unindexed, RLS-forced table on a shared 2-vCPU droplet seq-scans, and the work stalls on a migration that must index the largest table in the database. The insurance policy does not pay out.
findings.standard: Telemetry tables that exist for future analysis need the indexes the future analysis will use, plus a retention sweep, at creation time — the repo's own event_logs (90-day purge, three indexes) is the correct in-house precedent, and DECISIONS.md:2252 explicitly invoked it ('a rolling-purge à la event_logs can be added later if volume warrants') without a trigger, owner or metric.
findings.verifier_note: Severity: LOW (not medium), and the failure scenario as written is refuted - clip_impressions IS indexed on exactly (creator_id, shown_at) by migration 0037 (the models.py class merely fails to mirror it, minor ORM/DDL drift worth noting on its own). The 'write-only telemetry' framing is a recorded, reasoned deferral (DECISIONS.md [DEC #202], 2026-06-27). The accurate residual concern is data quality, not indexing or volume: routers/clips.py:857-877 inserts + commits on a GET, and frontend/src/pages/Review.tsx:239-246 polls that GET every 4s while any clip renders, so one viewing session writes ~150 duplicate rows per clip. Any future IPS/counterfactual analysis will need dedup-by-session or it will systematically over-weight videos that rendered slowly. Secondary and genuinely open: no retention sweep exists (unlike event_logs' 90-day purge), and the mid-handler commit means list_clips can never be served read-only.

findings.title: Six versioned JSONB payloads, no upcaster anywhere, and the geometry reader degrades to a plausible wrong answer on version mismatch
findings.evidence: clip_engine/edits.py:306,329-331 (GEOMETRY_DOC_VERSION; mismatch returns None); clip_engine/edits.py:79,218 (ClipEditDocument rejects newer versions — opposite behaviour); clip_engine/reframe.py:1058 (TRACK_JSON_VERSION); ingestion/signals.py:119; ingestion/peaks.py:170; routers/clips.py:317 (`has_baked_edits`); models.py:838-841 (style_preset drift, Issue 442 phantom `background` key)
findings.failure_scenario: Someone adds a field to the geometry document and bumps GEOMETRY_DOC_VERSION to 2 with no backfill (the precedent set by 0059's deliberate 'NO BACKFILL'). Every clip trimmed before that deploy still holds a v1 document. parse_geometry returns None for all of them, so _clip_response reports has_baked_edits:false and _clip_duration_s falls back to the SOURCE-window duration — the Review page now states a duration for a trimmed clip that does not match the video the creator will download, and denies the clip has baked edits when it does. Silently, for every historical row, with every test green. That is exactly the regression Issue 470 was filed to fix, re-introduced by a version bump, in a product whose stated identity is honesty.
findings.standard: The two recognised 2026 patterns are an in-payload version discriminator plus read-time upcasters, or expand→dual-write→parity-check→flip→drop applied inside the document. The load-bearing half is the upcaster: a version discriminator with no upcast path and no backfill is a latent silent-wrong-answer generator, not a versioning strategy. A single house rule for reject-vs-degrade is also needed — this repo currently does both.

findings.title: The unindexed-FK rule is written out in models.py and not applied to three creator_id columns
findings.evidence: models.py:958-963 (the rule, stated in full, on clip_edit_documents); models.py:1092-1104 (clip_impressions — no index beyond PK); models.py:1282-1298 (minute_deductions); video_feedback; migration 0037 (tenant_isolation RLS policy on clip_impressions)
findings.failure_scenario: DELETE /auth/me (right-to-erasure) fires the ON DELETE CASCADE on clip_impressions.creator_id. With no index, Postgres sequentially scans the whole table for every account deletion — and clip_impressions is the one table that grows without bound (see clip-impressions-write-only), so the erasure path gets monotonically slower over the life of the beta. Independently, the tenant_isolation RLS policy adds `creator_id = current_setting('app.creator_id')::uuid` to every query on the table, and with no index that qual can only be satisfied by a seq scan. minute_deductions and video_feedback are low-risk in practice (every production query on minute_deductions goes through UNIQUE(video_id) — billing/ledger.py:351, billing/refund.py:62, worker/tasks.py:401), so this is one real index and two cheap ones.
findings.standard: Postgres does not auto-index FK columns; an unindexed FK forces a seq scan of the child on every parent DELETE. The repo states this correctly at models.py:958-963 — the standard is already recorded here, just not applied uniformly.

findings.title: docs/MIGRATIONS.md Rule 2's NOT NULL recipe stops one step short of ever setting NOT NULL
findings.evidence: docs/MIGRATIONS.md:64-80 (Rule 2, two phases only); docs/MIGRATIONS.md:166-200 (Templates C and D); docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:142 (Rule 4's `UPDATE … LIMIT` is MySQL — already logged, still open); .github/workflows/ci.yml:255-300 (migration-lint advisory + path-filtered)
findings.failure_scenario: An author follows Templates C and D literally to make a column non-nullable, ships both deploys, and the column is never non-nullable — there is a validated CHECK constraint and no NOT NULL. alembic --autogenerate and every SQLAlchemy reader still see nullable=True. A later reader of models.py (or an AI session doing a CHECK-phase pass) sees `… | None`, concludes the invariant was never intended, and writes defensive `if x is None` branches for a case the schema was supposed to have eliminated. Related and worth adding to the existing OCB:142 row rather than re-filing: the only gate that would have caught the invalid Rule-4 backfill template is migration-lint, which is advisory and path-filtered, so the governing doc can stay wrong indefinitely while CI stays green — while migrations 0057 and 0062 both implement the correct CTE form and the context.is_offline_mode() branch.
findings.standard: The complete PG12+ recipe is four steps: ADD CONSTRAINT … CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID → VALIDATE CONSTRAINT → ALTER COLUMN … SET NOT NULL (which skips the table scan precisely because a valid CHECK proves it, per the PG12 commit 'Allow ALTER TABLE .. SET NOT NULL to skip provably unnecessary scans') → DROP CONSTRAINT. Steps 3 and 4 are the point of steps 1 and 2.
findings.verifier_note: I could not kill this. docs/MIGRATIONS.md:64-80 is headed 'New NOT NULL constraints - NOT VALID first, then VALIDATE' and shows exactly two phases, ending at `ALTER TABLE clips VALIDATE CONSTRAINT clips_creator_id_not_null`. Templates C (:166-181) and D (:183-200) are the same two steps in copy-paste form. Neither ever emits `ALTER COLUMN ... SET NOT NULL`, and neither drops the now-redundant CHECK. The claimed standard is the actual standard: PG12+ lets SET NOT NULL skip the table scan precisely because a validated CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) proves it, and the canonical published recipe is four steps (ADD ... NOT VALID -> VALIDATE -> SET NOT NULL -> DROP CONSTRAINT) - spot-checked against postgres.ai's 'How to add a CHECK constraint without downtime' and the pgsql mailing-list thread on SET NOT NULL skipping the scan, both of which give the same sequence and note VALIDATE's SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock is what makes it online-safe. The consequence is stated honestly and at the right severity (low): a follower gets a validated CHECK that does enforce the invariant in the database, but attnotnull is never set, so alembic --autogenerate and every SQLAlchemy/model reader still see nullable=True and downstream code accretes defensive None branches. Impact is latent rather than live - `grep 'NOT VALID' alembic/versions/*.py` returns zero hits, so Rule 2 has never been exercised, the identical shape to the already-logged Rule 4 defect (docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md, 2026-08-10 row: `UPDATE ... LIMIT` is MySQL, still Open), which supports appending to that row rather than re-filing. One nuance on the CI claim, which I checked rather than accepted: the Squawk step is genuinely gating inside its job (`exit $FAIL` at .github/workflows/ci.yml:361, with set -o pipefail), so 'advisory' is imprecise at the job level - but 'Migration lint (Squawk)' is NOT among the 8 required contexts listed in docs/BRANCHING.md:100-115, so a red result does not block merge. The characterisation is right in the way that matters (nothing forces the governing doc to be correct) even though the named mechanism is loose.

findings.title: Do NOT split the `clips` table — the four-lifecycle observation is real, the normalisation remedy is not
findings.evidence: models.py:728-894 (~25 columns); models.py:915-923 (the clip_edit_documents TOAST rationale); routers/clips.py:824-830; architecture-map.md B5/D2.6
findings.failure_scenario: If the ground-truth observation is read as a mandate, someone splits reframe_track_jsonb / signals_jsonb / the two geometry columns into satellite tables. That buys nothing measurable and costs joins, four more RLS policies to keep in sync, four more FK cascades on the erasure path, and four more chances to get the Issue-468-class CAS/confirm/discard transactions wrong — which the recorded history shows is exactly where this repo's SEV1s live. The clip_edit_documents split was correct because that document is written on a multi-second client autosave cadence with CAS revisions; reframe_track_jsonb is written once per render in the same transaction as render_uri, geometry once per confirm, signals_jsonb once at persist. None of them has the write profile that justified the original split.
findings.standard: Column count is not what costs anything in Postgres — TOASTed column *fetches* are, and only when actually fetched. The 2026 hybrid guidance promotes a JSONB key to a column when it is filtered on or updated independently of the rest of the document; none of these are. The measured problem is a SELECT list, not a schema.

findings.title: COMPLIANCE.md IS the retention decision record (correcting the ground truth) — but dna_embeddings and eight other tables are absent from it
findings.evidence: docs/COMPLIANCE.md:89-124 (28-row Data Classes & Retention table); :100 rendered clips; :112 clip impressions; :113 chat conversations; transcripts row 'Until video deleted'; docs/COMPLIANCE.md:4 (the file's own update rule); zero hits for dna_embeddings, video_context, summaries, improvement_briefs, creator_insights, usage, minute_, preference_model in that file
