findings.standard: Direct-column tenant_id policies under FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with a non-BYPASSRLS app role is the correct shape (this project implements it). The coverage set must be a derived property asserted against the catalog, not a hand-maintained list — otherwise the guard silently shrinks as the schema grows, which has already happened twice here.

findings.title: The 30-day YouTube purge is real and correct for four tables, and leaves a verbatim frozen copy of the same analytics in creator_dna, which is never deleted
findings.evidence: worker/tasks.py:4321-4410 (purge matches docs/COMPLIANCE.md:19-40 claim-for-claim); dna/builder.py:229-235 and :331-345 write views / engagement_rate / avg_view_duration_s / retention_spike_times / top_avg_views into patterns_jsonb; dna/profile.py:5 'DNA profiles are versioned and never deleted'; no DNA entry in worker/schedule.py's beat schedule; docs/COMPLIANCE.md:105 classifies all of DNA as 'Creator-owned derivative data / Until creator deletes' with no analysis; COMPLIANCE.md:93-96 still says 'Refresh cadence TBD — confirm from ToS' for four rows that COMPLIANCE.md:19-40 resolved on 2026-05-31
findings.failure_scenario: A beta creator disconnects their channel at myaccount.google.com. refresh_youtube_analytics stops advancing fetched_at. On day 30 the four analytics tables are purged and the log reads 'Purged stale YouTube analytics — metrics=N ...'. creator_dna.patterns_jsonb still holds their per-video view counts, engagement rates and retention-spike timestamps forever, plus dna_embeddings derived from the brief. III.D.2.3 requires deleting all API Data for a user whose token cannot be refreshed. The YouTube API Services compliance audit is triggered by the quota-extension request this project intends to make (COMPLIANCE.md:47-49).
findings.standard: III.E.4.b (fetched 2026-08-17) permits storing YouTube Analytics data and view-count statistics INDEFINITELY provided authorization is re-verified every 30 days — so the project's purge is stricter than required for active creators. The obligation that bites is III.D.2.3: on revocation or unrefreshable token, delete all API Data for that user. III.E.4.h separately bars using API Data to create new or derived metrics.

findings.title: Erasure discards the purge result: an Object-Lock-refused R2 delete leaves media alive with no DB pointer, unreachable by any later sweep
findings.evidence: worker/erasure.py:177-199 — purge_uris returns only the successes and its docstring says 'the caller must keep the DB pointer for any URI NOT in the returned set so a later sweep or a repeated erase can retry it'; routers/auth.py:513-520 logs len(purged)/len(uris), discards the return value, and proceeds to session.delete(creator) + commit() regardless; COMPLIANCE.md:100 confirms clips/ carries an R2 Object Lock window and that the intended posture is 'the DB pointer is kept and the retention sweep retries'
findings.failure_scenario: A creator with a clip rendered inside the R2 Object Lock window calls DELETE /auth/me. The delete for clips/{clip_id}.mp4 returns 403; purge_uris logs a warning and omits it; the clips row cascades away; append_audit(action='creator.deleted') is written; the endpoint returns 204. The MP4 — the creator's face and voice — now lives in R2 with no row referencing it and no prefix that would reach it (clips/ is deliberately non-creator-scoped). scripts/reapply_erasures.py cannot help: it replays erase_creator for RESURRECTED creator rows, and this creator was never resurrected. Nothing in the repo will ever find that object again.
findings.standard: GDPR Art. 17 erasure must be verifiable end to end, not best-effort-and-forget. The standard pattern where a delete can be legitimately refused (object lock / legal hold) is a durable tombstone or retry queue so a later sweep can complete it — which is exactly what this module's own docstring prescribes and the caller does not honour.

domains.verdict_headline: The deploy pipeline is above standard for this scale — the data-bearing staging gate, RepoDigest rollback target, and a rollback that still exits non-zero beat most funded teams. Observability is inverted: three telemetry rails are code-complete and none reaches a consumer, while the alerting layer a solo responder actually needs does not exist. The single VM is the right call and should not be revisited; the real bill is 0%-armed backups, an uptime probe that likely cannot exist on the current Cloudflare plan, and no browser-reachable staging URL — together under $10/month and half a day to close.
strengths: The data-bearing staging gate (deploy.yml:31-147): exact sha- image never :latest, migration against a PERSISTENT volume, an `alembic current == heads` assertion, and `stop` not `down` so the volume survives — four choices each traceable to a real incident, documented inline. Stronger than industry norm at this scale.

Auto-rollback still exits 1 (DECISIONS.md:11492 — 'rollback without exit 1 would hide the deployment failure from alerting'), the rollback target is captured as an immutable RepoDigest not a tag (deploy.yml:299-302), and `docker image prune` was deliberately moved AFTER the smoke so the rollback target survives.
`sync_secret` never blanks an existing VM value when a GitHub secret is unset (deploy.yml:243-247) — the difference between a partial secret set and an outage.
STORAGE_BACKEND=r2 is pinned authoritatively rather than defaulted, with the reason inline: a two-container topology makes local disk a broken backend. Written after it broke in production.

The DR design (DECISIONS.md:2327-2390) is textbook: Object Lock Compliance-vs-Governance reasoning, the circular-dependency constraint on key escrow, retention via R2 lifecycle so a script bug cannot mass-delete, `-pass env:` to keep the passphrase out of argv, and a MANDATORY reapply_erasures.py step after any restore — a GDPR subtlety most teams miss. It only needs switching on.

tests/test_ci_config.py asserts properties of the deploy YAML itself (dump precedes alembic, prod needs deploy-staging, staging is sha-pinned, compose parity) — testing the pipeline as an artifact is unusual, correct, and the only mechanism in the repo capable of catching a Class-1 regression in deploy config.
unmade_decisions: One authoritative 'Deployment: current state and why' entry marking DECISIONS.md:2541 and :2563 (Render) SUPERSEDED. Four entries, two silently reversed, and render.yaml still armed with autoDeployTrigger in the trunk — this is now a live-config question, not documentation hygiene.

A stated RTO and RPO. docs/RUNBOOKS.md:648 literally reads 'measured RTO recorded here: ________'. The recorded 24h RPO (DECISIONS.md:2334) is correct and should simply be paired with an RTO and a drill date.

An alerting policy defining what pages versus what waits until morning, in terms of SIGNALS. docs/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md defines the ladder for incidents already known about; nothing defines how an incident becomes known. Minimum credible set: ONE page (third-party probe on the public /health, 2 consecutive fails) plus five digest-only signals (backup heartbeat via BACKUP_HEALTHCHECK_URL to healthchecks.io free, deploy-failed email which already fires, spend-guard trip through the existing notify/ rail, a Beat-computed 'oldest non-terminal video > 30 min' stall check, and DO disk > 80%).

Where business metrics are supposed to land. Prometheus counters, an OTel push rail that explicitly excludes them (observability.py:786-788), and a Grafana panel spec that queries them — three half-rails and no decision on which is canonical.
A deprecation policy for parked artifacts (already named at architecture-map.md D4-22, still open). render.yaml shows the cost of leaving it open is not theoretical.
Log retention and rotation on the VM. No entry, no config, unbounded by Docker default.
Whether staging should be continuously reachable, and by whom. Currently an accident of deploy.yml:146 rather than a decision — and Cloudflare Access free (50 seats) makes it a $0 choice.

A single-VM failure-domain position (architecture-map.md D4-17). The uptime-probe, log-rotation and backup findings are all downstream of nothing ever stating what the VM is allowed to lose, how fast that must be noticed, and who notices.

findings.title: The only continuous production signal is a Cloudflare feature not available on the Free plan
findings.evidence: docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:145-172 (designates Cloudflare Health Checks as owner of uptime monitoring); .github/workflows/health-check.yml:3-12 (schedule removed because of that designation); docs/EDGE_SECURITY.md:87 ("On the Free plan the only lever..." — present tense about this zone); docs/DECISIONS.md:12290-12294 (rate-limit design sized to Cloudflare FREE tier, 1 rule)
findings.failure_scenario: Droplet powers off or the tunnel deregisters at 02:00 Saturday; Cloudflare serves 530/1033. No probe fires because standalone Health Checks are Pro+ only, so the replacement for the removed GitHub cron was likely never provisionable. Outage discovered whenever the owner next opens the site — this already happened for up to 9 days (docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:104), and that post-mortem blamed the removed cron without ever asking whether the replacement existed. No health-check ID, notification destination, or evidence row exists anywhere in the repo.
findings.standard: An uptime monitor must not share a failure domain with the thing it reports on, and must be verifiable. Cloudflare's own availability table lists standalone Health Checks as Free = No. 2026 cheap options: Better Stack free (10 monitors/3-min), UptimeRobot Solo ~$7/mo (free tier is non-commercial-only since Oct 2024).
findings.verifier_note: Severity: MEDIUM (rising to launch-blocker for a non-friend audience, already tracked as #282). Accurate statement: docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:145-172 assigns continuous uptime monitoring to Cloudflare standalone Health Checks, a Pro+ feature (Free = 0 checks per developers.cloudflare.com/health-checks/), on a zone other docs describe as Free (docs/EDGE_SECURITY.md:87; DECISIONS Issue 286). No health-check id, notification destination, or config artifact exists in the repo. Consequently docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:128's claim that prod has 'only Cloudflare Health Checks on /health' is very likely false, and the docs/GO_LIVE.md:82 action item 'Cloudflare Health Check per docs/DEPLOYMENT.md' cannot be completed on the current plan. Drop the 9-day-outage evidence: that outage was an intentional owner poweroff and GO_LIVE.md:82 retracted the 'proven in production' framing. Fix: confirm the zone plan, correct DEPLOYMENT.md, and close #282 with an off-host vendor (Better Stack free / healthchecks.io) verified against Bot Fight Mode.

findings.title: All 12 business metrics are exported nowhere, and two runbooks depend on reading them
findings.evidence: config.py:1142-1150 (/metrics auto-disables without METRICS_TOKEN); docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:128 (METRICS_TOKEN unset in prod); observability.py:786-788 ("Do NOT create a second prometheus-client bridge here"); no scraper/agent in docker-compose.prod.yml; docs/RUNBOOKS.md:755-772; docs/GO_LIVE.md:84
findings.failure_scenario: An operator follows RUNBOOKS.md:755-772 (Monthly Cost Review) and runs the llm-cost-panel query `sum by (provider) (increase(llm_cost_usd_total[1d]))` plus the `r2_bytes_stored{prefix}` cross-check that exists to confirm the 72h ToS source-media purge is running. Both return no series, so the purge check silently never happens. Separately, a prompt-loop regression that 10x's Anthropic spend increments llm_cost_usd_total in-process and is read by nothing — invisible until the spend guard hits its own hard cap or the invoice arrives. This holds even if Grafana Cloud is fully live, because OTel exports auto-instrumentation signals, not the prometheus-client registry.
findings.standard: Metrics that no backend ingests are not observability. At this scale the correct move is to emit the alert from the code that already computes the number into the notification rail that already exists (notify/ + Resend), rather than standing up a scrape target — cheaper than what has already been built.
findings.verifier_note: Severity: MEDIUM. Accurate statement: all 12 prometheus-client instruments in observability.py are reachable only through main.py:476 /metrics, which config.py:1144-1150 auto-disables in production because METRICS_TOKEN is unset (docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:128) and is not synced by deploy.yml. That is consistent with DECISIONS Issue 326, which kept prometheus-client for local dev and chose OTLP push for prod, and observability.py:786-788 deliberately refuses a prometheus->OTel bridge, so Grafana Cloud never sees these series. The defect is therefore documentation-vs-design drift, not a missing scraper: docs/RUNBOOKS.md (monthly cost review) and docs/GO_LIVE.md:84 both prescribe PRODUCTION queries over llm_cost_usd_total / r2_bytes_stored{prefix} that can never return a series. Blast radius is bounded -- the R2 ToS-purge check degrades to the Cloudflare R2 Metrics tab, and LLM spend is hard-capped by billing/spend_guard.py. Fix: either set METRICS_TOKEN and point a scraper at it, or (cheaper) emit the two numbers through notify/ and correct the two docs.

findings.title: DR is designed to current standard and 0% armed; RPO is total loss and RTO is a literal blank
findings.evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md:2327-2390 (the DR design); scripts/backup_pg.sh:66-69 (hard-dies on missing BACKUP_R2_BUCKET); .github/workflows/deploy.yml:293-300 (warns and continues); docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:26 (BACKUP_R2_BUCKET never set); docs/RUNBOOKS.md:648 ("measured RTO recorded here: ________"); .env.example (BACKUP_HEALTHCHECK_URL absent — grep returns only BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY at :117)
findings.failure_scenario: The droplet is lost right now. Timed walk: detect = hours-to-days (see cf-healthcheck finding); reprovision + Docker + awscli = 20-30 min; restore /opt/autoclip/.env = 5 min or unrecoverable (escrow is an operator step with no evidence row); restore Postgres = never, no dump exists. Result: actual RTO ~1h to an EMPTY database; actual RPO = total loss of billing ledgers, preference_models (the trained taste — the product itself), creator_dna, clip_outcomes and consent records. The known off-course row frames this as 'migrations run without a safety dump'; the unstated consequence is that the same single variable gates the nightly cron, so there are no backups of any kind. BACKUP_HEALTHCHECK_URL, the dead-man's-switch that would reveal a silently-failing nightly cron, is missing from .env.example so the config SSOT never prompts for it.
findings.standard: RPO 24h / RTO 4h with a quarterly drill is the right target at this scale — which is exactly what DECISIONS.md:2334-2335 already decided (logical pg_dump, PITR only at larger scale). 2026 guidance warns explicitly against over-buying RPO, not under-arming it. Recovery testing quarterly minimum.
findings.verifier_note: Severity: HIGH on consequence, but reclassify as a KNOWN, OWNER-BLOCKED gate rather than a new finding -- docs/GO_LIVE.md:59-61 and :216-221, LEFT_OFF.md:115 ('No backups exist today') and docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:26 already state that no backups of any kind exist and that the RTO blank is unfilled. Correct the evidence line: .env.example DOES document BACKUP_R2_BUCKET at :116 and BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY at :117; the genuinely missing variable is BACKUP_HEALTHCHECK_URL (consumed by scripts/backup_pg.sh:32 and scripts/backup_redis.sh:19,46,92 as the dead-man's-switch), absent from .env.example -- that is the only new, code-side actionable item, and it is a small config-SSOT fix. The rest restates the #255/#256/#257/#258/#288 operator queue.

findings.title: doctor.py probes every paid dependency and none of the four 'silence' variables; both observability inits no-op silently
findings.evidence: scripts/doctor.py (526 lines; grep for SENTRY|OTEL|METRICS_TOKEN|BACKUP_R2 returns zero hits, while Postgres/Redis/Anthropic/Voyage/Deepgram/R2/Stripe are all live-probed); observability.py:654 (`if not dsn: return`); observability.py:748-750 (`if not endpoint: return  # strict no-op`); main.py:554-567 (/health exposes postgres/redis/storage/version only)
findings.failure_scenario: An unhandled exception starts firing in render_video_clips for every creator. Sentry is dormant because the GitHub secret was never set; nothing captures it; the deploy preflight reported 30 ok / 0 fail the day before. There is no layer — config validation, preflight, boot log, or /health — at which 'observability configured' is distinguishable from 'observability dormant'. This is structurally identical to OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:148, where doctor.py green-lit Stripe with a raw httpx.get through a 10-week total outage; the lesson was applied to Stripe and not to the surface whose entire job is to report silent failure. Answers audit question 4: whether Sentry/OTel are live CANNOT be determined from this repo — it requires `gh secret list -R reese8272/creatorclip | grep -E 'SENTRY_DSN|OTEL_EXPORTER'` plus `ssh creatorclip-vm "grep -c '^SENTRY_DSN=.\+' /opt/autoclip/.env"`.
findings.standard: A preflight that green-lights a subsystem it does not exercise is worse than no check (this project's own recorded rule). Init paths for optional telemetry should log one line on BOTH branches so a single grep of the boot log answers 'is it on?'.
findings.verifier_note: Severity: MEDIUM. Accurate statement: scripts/doctor.py (526 lines) live-probes every paid dependency but contains zero references to SENTRY_DSN, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, METRICS_TOKEN or BACKUP_R2_BUCKET; observability.py:654 and :749-751 both return silently when their env is empty and neither branch logs; main.py:553-567 /health exposes only postgres/redis/storage/version; deploy.yml:238-240 skips the secret-sync silently when the GitHub secret is unset. So no layer distinguishes 'configured' from 'dormant'. Note the adjacency the finding should acknowledge: docs/GO_LIVE.md:81 already marks logs/metrics/traces + error tracking CODE-GREEN with 'external verify pending'. The value is the concrete fix -- one INFO line on both branches of each init, plus a doctor.py 'Observability' section that WARNs on empty SENTRY_DSN / OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT / METRICS_TOKEN when ENV=production.

findings.title: The prod critical-journey smoke has a silent-skip branch the staging gate proves is unnecessary
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/deploy.yml:373-377 (`if [ -z "${CC_JWT_SECRET:-}" ]; then echo "WARNING: ... skipping critical journey smoke."`); contrast .github/workflows/deploy.yml:130-133 (staging runs `sh -c 'CC_JWT_SECRET="$JWT_SECRET_KEY" python scripts/llm_harness.py --flow core'` with no such branch); tests/test_ci_config.py (22 tests, none reference CC_JWT_SECRET)
findings.failure_scenario: CC_JWT_SECRET is rotated, unset, or never set after a repo re-creation. Every deploy prints a WARNING, exits 0, and reports 'Deploy → autoclip.studio' green on a bare /health 200 — the exact signal GO_LIVE.md has twice recorded as insufficient. Six weeks of deploys claim 'Critical journey smoke passed' coverage they never executed, and because deploy.yml carries no required status and no test pins the branch, the degradation is invisible. The staging gate 240 lines earlier already demonstrates the fix: read the secret from inside the container it just started.
findings.standard: A verification step must not have a branch that skips itself and reports success. Delete the branch, mirror the staging invocation, and add one test_ci_config.py assertion that the prod smoke step contains no 'skipping' string (~10 lines).
findings.verifier_note: Keep as written, with two fixes. Corrected citations: the skip branch is .github/workflows/deploy.yml:365-367 (not 373-377) and the staging invocation is deploy.yml:135-137 (not 130-133). Drop the sentence 'Six weeks of deploys claim Critical journey smoke passed coverage they never executed' -- whether secrets.CC_JWT_SECRET is set cannot be determined from the repo; the defect is that a skip is indistinguishable from a pass, not that a skip is known to be occurring. Worth adding to the fix: the branch prints a bare echo rather than ::warning::, so it does not even surface as a run annotation.

findings.title: Auto-rollback runs an unscoped `docker compose down`, destroying the tunnel and the database to swap an app image
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/deploy.yml:332-333 (`docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml down --timeout 30 || true` then `IMAGE_TAG=rollback ... up -d || true`); scripts/deploy.sh:84-85 (mirrored); docker-compose.prod.yml (cloudflared, postgres, redis, autoheal all in the same project)
findings.failure_scenario: A bad image ships, the smoke fails, rollback runs. `down` is unscoped, so the cloudflared container is destroyed and recreated — during the down window plus tunnel re-registration autoclip.studio returns HTTP 530 / error 1033 ('origin unregistered from tunnel'), the exact signature the team burned days diagnosing (OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:104, ISSUES_LOG 2026-07-03-01). Postgres is simultaneously stopped under any in-flight Celery task. If the follow-up `up -d` fails for any reason, `|| true` swallows it and the entire stack including the database stays down while the job reports one `exit 1` that reads as 'deploy failed', not 'site is dark'. Related trap: after a rollback any manual `docker compose up -d` on the VM without IMAGE_TAG set silently rolls FORWARD to the broken :latest via `${IMAGE_TAG:-latest}`.
findings.standard: Rollback blast radius should match the change being reverted. One-line fix: `IMAGE_TAG=rollback docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --force-recreate --no-deps app worker render-worker beat`. 2026 zero-downtime guidance for single-VM Compose (atomic route switch, connection draining, health-gated traffic) points the same direction.
findings.verifier_note: Verified verbatim and I could not find a decision covering it. .github/workflows/deploy.yml:332-333 inside _rollback_and_fail() is exactly 'docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml down --timeout 30 || true' followed by 'IMAGE_TAG=rollback docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d || true'. scripts/deploy.sh:84-85 is byte-identical. docker-compose.prod.yml defines app, worker, render-worker, beat, postgres, redis, cloudflared and autoheal in one project, so the unscoped down destroys the tunnel and the database container to swap an app image -- while the NORMAL deploy path one step earlier (deploy.yml:302) uses the correctly scoped 'up -d --remove-orphans'. The 530/1033 tunnel-re-registration signature is the one recorded at docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:104 / ISSUES_LOG 2026-07-03-01. The double '|| true' genuinely swallows a failed recreate, leaving the whole stack down behind a single exit 1. The forward-roll trap is real: docker-compose.prod.yml:3-7 interpolates ${IMAGE_TAG:-latest}, so a bare 'docker compose up -d' after a rollback relaunches :latest. I checked for a recorded decision: docs/DECISIONS.md:11482-11492 (Issue 271) describes the mechanism only as 're-pull + restart' and justifies the exit 1 and the no-blue-green choice -- blast radius is never discussed, so the down/up implementation is an unjustified deviation from the intent that entry records. No data loss (down without -v keeps the postgres volume), which the finding correctly does not claim. Severity medium is honest: it fires only on an already-failing deploy, but it converts 'bad image' into 'whole stack down, possibly silently'.

findings.title: No Docker log rotation anywhere; a full disk is a total outage on a single-VM failure domain
findings.evidence: grep for `logging:|max-size|max-file|json-file` across docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.prod.yml, docker-compose.staging.yml, render.yaml and deploy/ returns zero hits; no daemon.json is tracked; docker-compose.prod.yml runs 8 always-on containers including a Celery worker at --loglevel=info and two uvicorn workers emitting JSON access logs
findings.failure_scenario: /var/lib/docker/containers/*/*-json.log grows without bound (Docker's json-file max-size defaults to -1, unlimited) and fills the droplet volume over some months. Postgres cannot write WAL and refuses writes; every upload, render and billing grant fails; /health reports postgres:error so the app healthcheck fails and the autoheal sidecar restart-loops the app indefinitely. Recovery requires SSH — which in the one whole-droplet incident on record timed out with 100% ping loss. A five-minute config change prevents the single most plausible way this VM kills itself.
findings.standard: Docker Engine ships json-file rotation OFF by default; max-size/max-file must be set explicitly, per service or as daemon-level defaults. Pair with a free DigitalOcean disk-usage alert.

findings.title: render.yaml is not stale config — it carries autoDeployTrigger: commit alongside VERBOSE_LOGGING_ALLOW_PROD=true
findings.evidence: render.yaml:125, :153, :181 (`autoDeployTrigger: commit` on all three services); render.yaml:40-43 (VERBOSE_LOGGING=true + VERBOSE_LOGGING_ALLOW_PROD=true with ENV=production and LOG_DIR=""); docs/DECISIONS.md:2395 (a Render Postgres was provisioned and never cut over); docs/AUDIT_KNOWN_ISSUES.md:171-186 (classifies this as an operator check, not a code finding)
findings.failure_scenario: If the Render Blueprint is still linked to main — which nothing in the repo confirms or denies — every push to main auto-deploys a second ENV=production copy of the application that streams raw prompts, raw LLM responses, full transcripts and full request bodies including PII into Render's log aggregator through a deliberately non-scrubbing formatter, bypassing redact.py. Secrets are sync:false so blast radius depends on which were entered once, and R2_BUCKET and STRIPE_SECRET_KEY are among them. Even if unlinked, the file has already misled the project once: Issue 326's brief was written against render.yaml and had to be re-scoped mid-issue (DECISIONS.md:2395). The autoDeployTrigger lines are what upgrade this from 'stale document' to 'deployment trigger sitting in the trunk of a push-to-deploy repo'.
findings.standard: Parked artifacts leave the trunk and live as a git tag. Note a factual correction to the audit premise: the 35MB .mp4 and dump.rdb are gitignored (.gitignore:41 and :34) and {{pkgetc}}/ is untracked working-directory cruft — none are in the repository. The 12 root PNGs are tracked (~1.7MB) but excluded from the Docker build context by .dockerignore's root-scoped *.png. The real committed debt is render.yaml + deploy/charts/ (12 files, never run) + the PNGs.
findings.verifier_note: Does not stand as a finding. Any residual is trivial hygiene, not a security or deploy risk: render.yaml + deploy/charts/ + 12 root PNGs (~1.0 MB, not 1.7 MB) are parked artifacts that would be tidier as a git tag. The autoDeployTrigger: commit lines are Render's documented default for new services and change nothing; the file is inert unless a Blueprint is linked in the Render dashboard, which is already logged as an owner check at docs/AUDIT_KNOWN_ISSUES.md:182-186 and whose retention was deliberately decided at docs/DECISIONS.md:2395.

findings.title: The staging gate is the best thing in the pipeline and no human can look at it
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/deploy.yml:146-147 (`stop app worker` after the gate, keeping only the volume); docs/STAGING_ACCESS.md:114 (only access path is `ssh creatorclip-vm 'curl -s http://localhost:8001/health'`); docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:121-141 ("Gate 2 — Manual smoke test", a six-item human checklist with nowhere to run)
findings.failure_scenario: A change lands that renders a failure string in success green (OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:22, review/YourCall.tsx:124) or draws a fabricated waveform under a real source timeline (:40). Every automated gate passes — the token was valid, just wrong — and the first human to see the rendered page is a beta user in production. Ground truth §B records CI catching under 1 in 10 defects and zero SEV1s, while Class 5 (honesty/UX inversion) and Class 10 (clip quality) escape to production by construction; those are exactly the classes a human eye on a rendered page catches. The pipeline automated what automation is bad at here and left the one human-effective check unreachable.
findings.standard: Fix costs $0: add a second Zero Trust ingress rule staging.autoclip.studio -> ccstage app:8000 on the tunnel that already runs, gate it with Cloudflare Access (free tier, 50 seats, full ZTNA on self-hosted apps), and change deploy.yml:146 from `stop app worker` to `stop worker`. Cost is ~1GB RAM on the droplet, no new vendor, no new bill.

findings.title: The single VM is the right call at this scale — moving to a PaaS costs ~2x and fixes nothing broken
findings.evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md:2473 (v1 locked to <=100-user private beta, 10k infra track DESCOPED); docker-compose.prod.yml (render-worker at --concurrency=1 because parallel ffmpeg encodes starve each other on a small box, Issue 432); docs/DECISIONS.md:10315 (VM + Compose, not Kubernetes)
findings.failure_scenario: Counterfactual, costed: Render equivalent = web + worker + beat instances + managed PG + Key Value ~= $110-130/mo on shared CPU that is worse for ffmpeg/MediaPipe, with an ephemeral filesystem hostile to the render pipeline's /tmp usage; Fly shared-CPU-4x ~= $42.79/mo but usage-billed and unpredictable with a steeper ops curve for zero benefit in one region; current DO 4 vCPU/8 GiB ~= $48/mo flat. A migration would consume weeks and leave the backups unarmed, the uptime probe absent and staging unreachable — the three things that actually hurt. Total honest spend to close all three on the CURRENT topology: under $10/month and about half a day. Also aligned: the absence of a human approval step in deploy.yml is current standard, not a gap, given a real pre-prod gate plus automated rollback (DORA elite = deploy on demand, recover under an hour).
findings.standard: DO/flat pricing is the recommended choice when cost predictability beats global distribution; PaaS is not indicated for CPU-bound video workloads at one region. Trunk-based + automated rollback, not manual approval, is the 2026 shape for small teams.

domains.verdict_headline: The ledger core is the strongest code in this repo — SAVEPOINT+UNIQUE idempotency on both directions of the balance, a correct transactional-outbox notification listener, and a bidirectional AST sweep that structurally forbids an unbilled Anthropic call. The Stripe boundary is where it is still thin: entitlement is granted from metadata.pack_id alone and `amount_total` is never read or stored, so `MinutePack.price_cents` is a copy of a compile-time constant and amount reconciliation is structurally impossible, not merely absent. Most importantly for a process audit: the defect that kept billing dead for its entire life (webhook registered at a path the app does not serve) was fixed by hand in the Stripe Dashboard and has no mechanism preventing recurrence.
strengths: billing/ledger.py idempotency is structural rather than conventional: grant_minutes and deduct_for_video are mirror images (fast-path SELECT → begin_nested SAVEPOINT → flush to force the INSERT and surface the UNIQUE conflict now → IntegrityError → clean no-op), and the balance update is a single conditional `UPDATE … WHERE minutes_balance >= minutes RETURNING` with no read-modify-write. Critically, grant_minutes:314-320 RE-RAISES IntegrityError when stripe_session_id is None, because a non-keyed grant has no UNIQUE to race on and swallowing it would silently give a new beta user 0 trial minutes (Issue 76) — that distinction is what separates an idempotency handler from a bug-swallower, and it is explained in the code.

tests/test_usage_coverage.py is the best gate in the repo and the reason 'every LLM call is billed' is a fact rather than a hope: it is a BIDIRECTIONAL AST sweep — `discovered - mapped` fails on a new unbilled Anthropic call site, and `mapped - discovered` fails on a stale map entry. The staleness half is what most such gates omit and is why this one cannot rot into a vacuous pass. Layer 2 exists because layer 1's per-function grep could not see chat/intake.py or knowledge/thumbnails.analyze_thumbnail_patterns, and the evidence marker for the latter ('_patterns_usage,') is deliberately narrowed so the sibling concepts-billing line cannot satisfy it.

The ledger.py after_commit/after_rollback listener pair (:37-67) is a correct transactional outbox: balance_low notifications are staged in session.info and drained only on commit, with a rollback handler that discards them — closing the 'notified for a deduction a later rollback undid' hole, as a class-level listener with no per-call bookkeeping.

model_rates() falls back to OPUS rates (the highest in the price book) for unknown model families with the reasoning stated in-code — 'so a misconfigured model never under-bills against the spend guard'. Failing expensive rather than cheap on the money path is the right default and is rarely gotten right. Relatedly, record_llm_usage orders its rails correctly: the Prometheus counter + spend-guard tap run in the first try block and the DB ledger write in a second, so cost control survives a DB failure.

spend_guard._record_and_enforce releases the SETNX trip latch when _flip_llm_flag raises (:346-353) — 'A latch with no flip would silence the breaker for the full cool-down TTL while the breach keeps burning.' That is precisely the failure mode a naive latch has, anticipated and closed. And the per-creator arm can never trip the global switch (:299-317): one creator's runaway gets a cool-down key; only global/velocity arms touch llm_generation.

Two Stripe details that are tighter than the reference and say why: the idempotency key is tenant-prefixed as `checkout:{creator_id}:{intent_id}` with the account-wide key-collision hazard spelled out (stripe_client.py:140-147), and the webhook narrows payment_status to == 'paid' rather than Stripe's != 'unpaid', with the reason stated (every PURCHASABLE_PACKS entry has price_cents > 0, so no_payment_required is not a valid outcome). The webhook rate limit also correctly sits IN FRONT of signature verification so a bad-signature flood cannot burn threads on HMAC.
unmade_decisions: A single 'money-path assertions' entry in docs/DECISIONS.md. The 10-week outage produced the right lesson — 'provider says paid' and 'app granted entitlement' are two independently checkable assertions — but it lives in snag-taxonomy.md and GO_LIVE.md prose. §A7 has 13 billing entries and none states the principle, so each new money surface re-derives it or doesn't.

Which Stripe events this app subscribes to, and why the rest are excluded. Today the answer is implicit in one `if` at routers/billing.py:245. It should be an explicit list — checkout.session.completed, the async pair, the refund/dispute set — with the deliberately-unhandled ones named as deliberate.

Whether the Stripe payment-method set is code-controlled or Dashboard-controlled. Today it is Dashboard-controlled by omission (payment_method_types is unset). Either position is defensible; the undeclared one is not.

What MinutePack.price_cents means — catalog price or amount collected. It currently means the former while reading like the latter. One sentence settles it and dictates whether amount_total and currency become columns.

A reconciliation objective. reconcile_stripe_ledger exists (Issue 205) but no entry states what divergence it detects, in which direction, at what latency, or who is told. As built it is a Stripe→ledger REPAIR job, not a DETECTOR — its `errors` counter writes logger.error into a log with no alert rule and no scrape target.

A cache-floor-per-model policy. config.py holds a 20-entry model registry and tests/test_model_config.py bans hardcoded model literals, yet the cacheable-prefix floor is a hardcoded global in two files. Either derive it from the configured model (mirroring model_rates()), or record why one conservative floor is preferred.

A cost-of-goods position beyond Anthropic. record_llm_usage is an excellent choke point for ANTHROPIC spend; Deepgram (COST_PER_MIN_DEEPGRAM=0.0097), Voyage, R2 egress and ffmpeg CPU are priced in config.py and none is in the ledger or visible to the spend guard. At the Stream pack's 4.0 c/min, Deepgram alone is ~24% of revenue per minute — the margin model exists in packs.py's docstring and nothing measures it. Not urgent at 100 users, but 'the spend guard covers Anthropic only' should be a written scope boundary.

When a '📋 Open' money-path row in OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md gets force-triaged. A money row sat stale ~8 weeks after its fix shipped and propagated a false claim into this audit's own ground truth. A rule as blunt as 'money-path rows are re-verified at every close-out' would have caught it.

findings.title: Nothing verifies the Stripe-registered webhook endpoint resolves to a route this app serves
findings.evidence: scripts/doctor.py (grep 'webhook' → 0 hits); scripts/*.py (grep 'webhook_endpoints' → 0 hits); routers/billing.py:220; tests/test_issue_110.py:44-57; tests/test_static.py:1038-1070; docs/GO_LIVE.md:91 (Issue 485b)
findings.failure_scenario: Any future action that re-creates the Stripe endpoint — rotating the signing secret by delete+re-add, adding a staging endpoint, or moving the router prefix — restores the exact 2026-05-31→08-12 outage: POST /billing/checkout returns 200, the customer is charged, `billing_webhook_received` never fires, and nothing inside the app can observe it. The three tests that mention the path all assert properties of routers/billing.py source or the app's own route table; none can see Stripe's side of the contract. doctor.py was hardened for the TRANSPORT half of that same incident (OFF_COURSE_BUGS:148) and not the ROUTING half. One API call closes it: `_STRIPE.webhook_endpoints.list()` returns `url` and `enabled_events`; assert each URL's path is in FastAPI's route table and that enabled_events covers the handled set.
findings.standard: Stripe's fulfillment guide (docs.stripe.com/checkout/fulfillment, fetched 2026-08-17) states webhooks are REQUIRED for fulfillment and cannot be replaced by the landing-page redirect. The repo's own derived lesson (snag-taxonomy.md §D-1) is 'a test that reads the app's own route table and pins the webhook path' — written down, never made structural.
findings.verifier_note: Real but lower-severity gap: no automated check asserts that the endpoint registered in Stripe resolves to a route this app serves, so a delete-and-re-add of the endpoint, a staging endpoint, or a router-prefix move silently re-breaks webhook delivery with no test or gate failing. Severity LOW-MEDIUM, not high: `reconcile_stripe_ledger` (worker/schedule.py:87, daily, 48h `created[gte]` lookback) grants minutes for any paid card session missing a ledger row, so the concrete consequence is up to ~24h delayed fulfillment plus loss of the `billing_webhook_received` signal - and grants arriving with `reason="reconcile"` instead of `"purchase"` are themselves observable. This does NOT reproduce the 2026-05-31->08-12 outage, which was the transport defect (Issue 453); a routing-only regression reproduces 485b alone. The proposed fix (`_STRIPE.webhook_endpoints.list()` -> assert each URL path is in FastAPI's route table and `enabled_events` covers the handled set) remains the right closure and is one API call. Worth pairing with a check that the reconcile sweep has actually fired in prod, since it is currently an unexercised backstop.

findings.title: A Stripe Dashboard toggle creates a take-money-grant-nothing path the 48h reconcile sweep cannot catch
findings.evidence: billing/stripe_client.py:93-116 (no payment_method_types); routers/billing.py:245-260 (only checkout.session.completed; async_payment_succeeded named in comment at :256, no branch); billing/stripe_client.py:173,180 (created[gte] = now - lookback); config.py:881 (STRIPE_RECONCILE_LOOKBACK_HOURS=48); .env.example:299
findings.failure_scenario: Owner enables ACH Direct Debit in the Stripe Dashboard (a UI toggle — no code change, no deploy, no review, because payment_method_types is unpinned). Creator buys Stream ($400.00 / 10,000 min) on day 0. checkout.session.completed fires with payment_status='unpaid'; routers/billing.py:259 correctly returns {'status':'ignored'}. ACH settles day 4; checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded fires; no branch handles it. The daily sweep on day 4 queries created[gte]=day 2 — the session was CREATED on day 0, so it is outside the window, and further outside on every later day. Net: $400 collected, 0 minutes granted, permanently, and `errors` in worker/tasks.py:4717-4728 never increments because the session is never returned. AUDIT_KNOWN_ISSUES §D names the unhandled event; the new signal is that the trigger is a Dashboard toggle and that the reconcile fallback is keyed on session-creation rather than settlement time so it cannot backstop it.
findings.standard: Stripe's reference handler branches on BOTH checkout.session.completed AND checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded, verbatim, and states 'Automatic fulfillment with webhooks is required if you ... accept payment methods with delayed success notification, because their subsequent state changes only after the Checkout Session completes.'
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed as stated. Only nuance worth carrying into the writeup: the path is latent rather than live (ACH/BNPL not currently enabled), so read the severity as 'high the moment a delayed-notification method is enabled, and enabling it takes one Dashboard toggle with zero code review'. The two-line fix is to branch on `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded` alongside `completed`, and to pin `payment_method_types=["card"]` so enabling a delayed method becomes a code change rather than a Dashboard click.

findings.title: MinutePack.price_cents is a copy of a compile-time constant; amount_total is never read, so amount reconciliation is impossible by construction
findings.evidence: routers/billing.py:306-314 (price_cents=pack.price_cents); billing/ledger.py:302; billing/packs.py:61 (Pack('stream','Stream',10000,40000)); cs['amount_total'] / cs['currency'] / cs['amount_subtotal'] appear nowhere in the repo
findings.failure_scenario: Owner creates a $1.00 promo Payment Link in the Stripe Dashboard and, following the metadata convention visible in their own prod logs, sets metadata[creator_id]=<uuid> and metadata[pack_id]=stream. Payment Links emit checkout.session.completed to the same endpoint. The handler reads pack_id='stream', looks up 10,000 minutes / 40000 cents, and grants 10,000 minutes while writing price_cents=40000 — a $1.00 payment books as $400.00 of revenue and 400x the entitlement, with a ledger row that can never contradict it. AUDIT_KNOWN_ISSUES §D calls this 'a ledger-accuracy gap'; that understates it — the column is a constant, so no query over the ledger can ever disagree with the catalog and no reconciliation against Stripe's balance or payout report is possible on amount. Fix caution: a naive amount_total != price_cents check false-positives under STRIPE_TAX_ENABLED (stripe_client.py:136-138 adds tax on top) or Adaptive Pricing currency conversion — compare amount_subtotal with a currency=='usd' guard, and store amount_total+currency regardless.
findings.standard: Current practitioner guidance: 'verify the amount_total matches your expected amount before recording the purchase and fulfilling the order.' The generalised form — 'provider says paid' and 'app granted entitlement' are two independently checkable assertions — is this repo's own derived lesson from the 10-week outage (snag-taxonomy.md §D-1) and is not implemented.
findings.verifier_note: Real but low-severity, and largely a restatement of docs/AUDIT_KNOWN_ISSUES.md section D. Accurate version: the MinutePack ledger stores the catalog constant (`price_cents=pack.price_cents`, routers/billing.py:313) and the repo never reads `amount_total`/`amount_subtotal`/`currency` anywhere, so revenue in the ledger can never be reconciled against Stripe's balance or payout report. It is not exploitable by any creator - there is no path for a customer to influence session metadata - and promo codes are off (`allow_promotion_codes` unset, Stripe default false), so no discount can currently produce a divergence. The residual risk is owner self-inflicted mispricing (a hand-built Payment Link or Dashboard-created session with `pack_id` metadata), plus permanent inability to audit. The Stripe fulfillment doc does NOT prescribe an `amount_total` check - drop that attribution; the defensible framing is 'record what was actually collected so provider-says-paid and app-granted-entitlement are two independently checkable assertions'. Fix remains cheap and correct: store `amount_total` + `currency` on the ledger row (comparing `amount_subtotal` under a `currency == 'usd'` guard if a mismatch alert is added, to avoid false positives from `STRIPE_TAX_ENABLED` at stripe_client.py:136-138). Severity LOW, not medium.

findings.title: Refunds and chargebacks reported by Stripe are unhandled, and reconciliation runs only Stripe→ledger
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'charge\.|dispute|payment_intent' routers/ worker/ billing/ → no handler for charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created, charge.dispute.funds_withdrawn, payment_intent.payment_failed; worker/tasks.py:4622-4728 (sweep is one-directional); docs/DECISIONS.md:4141 (Issue 208)
findings.failure_scenario: A creator buys Stream ($400.00 / 10,000 min), consumes 8,000 minutes over three weeks, then files a card chargeback. Stripe withdraws $400 plus the dispute fee. The MinutePack row stays, Creator.minutes_balance keeps 2,000 minutes, the creator keeps rendering, and no code path anywhere observes the event. At beta scale one such event is the entire month's revenue. DECISIONS:4141 (Issue 208) is a recorded decision covering refunds the BUSINESS initiates (discretionary, ledger-append-only, runbook-driven) — it says nothing about refunds and disputes Stripe REPORTS, which is the case that costs money. The reverse-direction sweep gap is the same shape: _reconcile_stripe_ledger_async only grants what Stripe says was paid and the ledger lacks; a MinutePack row whose session was refunded, disputed, or never existed is invisible.
findings.standard: Stripe's fulfillment guide directs listening for async_payment_failed and, for entitlement products, the refund/dispute event set is the standard clawback trigger. The compensating-row pattern is already documented in this repo at billing/refund.py:18-26 ('money_refund:{stripe_session_id}', negative minutes) — the decision covers initiating one, not detecting one.

findings.title: Prompt-cache floor hardcoded to Sonnet 4.6's 1024 tokens, but the three most expensive calls run Opus 5, whose minimum is 512
findings.evidence: knowledge/util.py:36 (_CACHE_FLOOR_TOKENS=1024) applied at :77; clip_engine/scoring.py:103 (_CACHE_FLOOR_CHARS=4*1024) applied at :403; both documented against Sonnet 4.6 at scoring.py:98-99 and util.py:61-62; config.py:117,141,145 set ANTHROPIC_MODEL_SCORING/VIDEO_CONTEXT/CLIP_METADATA to claude-opus-5 per DECISIONS.md:921 §6 (2026-08-05); DECISIONS.md:2837 (Issue 315) set the 1024 floor for Sonnet 4.6 on 2026-06-24 and was never revisited
findings.failure_scenario: A creator with a compact DNA brief yields a combined static-corpus + DNA prefix of ~700 estimated tokens (~2,800 chars). scoring.py:403 computes 2800//4 = 700 >= 1024 → False → no cache_control is attached. Every score_candidates call for that creator pays full $5/MTok Opus 5 input on ~700 prefix tokens that Opus 5 would have served at $0.50/MTok — 100% of the achievable saving on that block, forgone, on the highest-volume highest-cost call in the system, and identically on video_context and clip_metadata. The gate is silently conservative: cached_write_1h (scoring.py:455) confirms the marker LANDED, not that it should have been SENT, so no test or metric can distinguish 'cached' from 'declined to try'. Structurally the issue is a single global constant encoding one model's floor in a codebase whose model registry is 20 per-task entries with tests/test_model_config.py banning hardcoded model literals — the floor should derive from the configured model the way billing.ledger.model_rates() already derives per-model pricing. Compounding: chars//4 is a Sonnet-calibrated heuristic and Opus 5 uses the Opus 4.7-generation tokenizer, so estimate and threshold are mis-tuned in the same direction.
findings.standard: Anthropic's prompt-caching docs (current): minimum cacheable prefix is 512 tokens for Claude Opus 5, 1024 for Sonnet 4.6, 4096 for Haiku 4.5 — explicitly non-monotonic, with the docs calling out that 'Claude Opus 5 halves the Opus 4.8 minimum (1024 → 512), so prompts previously too short to cache now create entries with no code change.' Cache reads bill 0.1x; 1h writes 2x. Opus 5 is $5/$25 per MTok.
findings.verifier_note: Not a finding. The exact tradeoff is a recorded decision: docs/DECISIONS.md:969-971 (2026-08-05, 'Opus 5 for the clip-quality chain', section 6) states the 1024 gates were deliberately NOT lowered to Opus 5's 512 minimum because the floor helper is shared with Sonnet callers where 512 would emit inert 2x cache writes, and explicitly accepts that a 512-1024-token prefix on Opus merely misses caching. config.py:116 already records the 512 minimum. The finding's premise that Issue 315's 1024 'was never revisited' is false. If anything is worth filing it is a much smaller, non-'deviation' cleanup: clip_engine/scoring.py:103's `_CACHE_FLOOR_CHARS` is Opus-5-only and is not covered by the shared-helper half of that rationale, so it could derive its floor from the configured model the way `billing.ledger.model_rates()` already derives pricing. Economic value of doing so is roughly $0.003 per score_candidates call - single-digit dollars over the whole beta. Severity: informational/nit.

findings.title: Spend guard fails open correctly, but its failure emits no rail, and Redis is a single point of failure for every cost control simultaneously
findings.evidence: billing/spend_guard.py:112-119 (_warn_fail_open: module-global set, logger.warning only — no counter, no log_event, no record_event, unlike _emit_spend_event's dual rail at :167-182); config.py:1144-1150 (/metrics auto-disables in prod without METRICS_TOKEN, which is unset — OFF_COURSE_BUGS:128); grep alert docs/dashboards/ → 0 hits; limiter.py:148-149; config.py:974-987; docker-compose.prod.yml:46,72
findings.failure_scenario: Redis flaps. record_spend, creator_block_status, AND slowapi's per-creator daily quota all fail open at once on the one shared dependency (limiter.py:148-149 documents this verbatim). The global breaker also dies, because tripping llm_generation requires record_spend to fire, which requires Redis. The only signal is one logger.warning per worker process for its lifetime, into a log with no alert rule and no scrape target. Worst-case burn: the Opus 5 chain is ~$0.60/video (video_context ~20k in/2k out = $0.15; score_candidates ~25k in/4k out = $0.23; clip_metadata ~10k in/3k out = $0.13; plus Sonnet extras); the general queue runs --concurrency=4 at ~5-10 min/pipeline = 24-48 videos/hour → ~$15-30/hour. Against SPEND_CAP_GLOBAL_DAILY_USD=50 and SPEND_CAP_GLOBAL_MONTHLY_USD=400 that exceeds the daily cap in 2-3 hours and the monthly cap in under a day. Honestly: bounded, not catastrophic — worker concurrency is the real backstop and a saturated queue at 100 beta users is implausible. The finding is that the guard can be non-functional for weeks with no signal, the same shape as health-check.yml's schedule that 'silently died 2026-06-17 and nobody noticed'. One SPEND_GUARD_FAILOPEN_TOTAL counter plus one record_event on first fail-open makes it detectable.
findings.standard: Fail-open on the cost-control path is the correct posture at this scale and matches flags.py — I am not disputing it. Current SRE practice for a fail-open safety control is that the OPEN state must itself be an observable, alertable signal, otherwise the control is indistinguishable from a working one. The repo already has the right pattern in-file (_emit_spend_event's dual log+DB rail for breaches) and simply does not apply it to the guard's own failure.

findings.title: OFF_COURSE_BUGS:70 'cached tokens billed 0x' is FIXED and has been stale ~8 weeks; the audit's own ground truth inherited the false claim
findings.evidence: billing/ledger.py:148-153 prices all four tiers using COST_CACHE_READ_MULTIPLIER and cache_write_multiplier; record_llm_usage:231-233 threads cache_read/cache_creation; ttl:1h callers pass 2.0 at worker/tasks.py:653, :812, routers/clips.py:2323; chat/runner.py:196-203 passes both cache fields into _estimate_cost_usd; fix shipped same-day per docs/DECISIONS.md:3007 (2026-06-24); row still reads '📋 Open — awaiting approval (money path)'; snag-taxonomy.md §A class 8 lists it as a live leak
findings.failure_scenario: Not a code failure — a record failure with a concrete consequence already realised: this audit's own ground-truth pack (snag-taxonomy.md class 8) carries the stale claim forward as a live money-path leak, and any reader triaging by 'money rows first' would spend effort re-fixing shipped code. Revenue impact of the underlying bug going forward is zero. Its remaining significance is as evidence for snag-taxonomy.md §E-3 (the off-course log has no closing pressure) — and a money-path row is the worst one to leave stale, because readers reasonably assume money rows are triaged first. Residual sub-severity: chat/runner.py:196 omits cache_write_multiplier so it defaults to 1.25x; if chat ever attaches a ttl:'1h' marker its cache writes under-bill by 0.75x on write tokens only.
findings.standard: A defect log is only load-bearing if closed items are closed. Standard practice is that the fix commit closes the row; here the fix landed the same day the row was written and the row was never touched. A rule as blunt as 're-verify money-path rows at every close-out' would have caught it.

domains.verdict_headline: The suite is well-written and genuinely asserts (I measured: 18 of 3,102 test functions lack any assertion, ~15 of those legitimately) — but the gates are aimed at the wrong risk class: every required check verifies the maintainer's code against the maintainer's fixtures, while all three multi-week outages lived at the seam with systems nobody here controls. Worse, I found instance #5 of the vacuous-green class inside this domain: the mutation gate — the only mechanism measuring whether tests assert rather than merely execute — has never executed a single mutant in its life while reporting success on 8/8 weekly runs. The fix set is small: ~10-13 maintainer-hours closes the class that has cost 24 weeks of dead subsystems.
strengths: tests/test_data_api.py:44-240 — the fields= projection simulator is better than what most teams ship: it reimplements Google's partial-response grammar, PINS THE SIMULATOR ITSELF against Google's documented example (test_fields_simulator_matches_googles_documented_semantics), then applies the real _FIELDS_* constants to the fixtures before parsing. The 'pin the measuring instrument' step is the one almost everyone skips.

tests/test_scoring_goldens.py — real recorded Anthropic bodies deserialized back through anthropic.types.Message so SDK drift fails the test, a genuine stop_reason='max_tokens' golden recorded by re-issuing at max_tokens≈200, and a sha256 pin of _OUTPUT_SCHEMA so a golden can never green-stamp a contract it wasn't recorded against. Worth copying into other projects.

The anti-hollowing pattern is correct and generalizable verbatim: SCENARIO_FLOOR (tests/test_clip_engine.py:269) + the skip-marker regex scan (:301) + a SECOND pin in a different file (tests/test_eval_transparency.py:101-110) so lowering the floor must touch two files and shows up in any diff. Generalize to: a MUTANT_FLOOR on the mutation run, a floor on _TENANT_TABLES, a floor on _ANTHROPIC_CALL_SITES, and a REQUIRED_CHECK_FLOOR.

The registry + AST-sweep family is the project's real innovation and already fails CI on the NEXT instance rather than the last one: tests/test_usage_coverage.py (next unbilled Anthropic call site), tests/test_llm_conformance.py (singleton/timeout/typed-exception/untrusted-content-policy per LLM module), tests/test_ci_config.py (22 tests over the CI/CD YAML itself).

The RLS integration lane is done correctly INCLUDING the lesson from its own past failure: tests/test_rls_isolation_integration.py explicitly SET LOCAL ROLE creatorclip_app (:308, :355, :397, :428…) so policies are evaluated under the non-bypass role rather than the container owner, and test_rls_deny_by_default_unset_context (:405-444) now iterates _TENANT_TABLES rather than the hardcoded 2-tuple that made OFF_COURSE :25 vacuous. The fix stuck.

Assertion quality is NOT the problem — measured, not assumed. AST sweep over all 3,102 collected test functions: 18 (0.6%) have no assertion of any kind, and ~15 of those are legitimate 'must not raise' tests for fail-open paths (test_spend_guard.py:212,229; test_usage_ledger.py:214; test_observability.py:409). Do not spend effort on assertion-density linting here. Also: llm-e2e-nightly.yml:88-91 and :120-121 handle ${PIPESTATUS[0]} exactly right, and the nightly transcription_live leg (re-transcribe a real LibriSpeech fixture against live Deepgram, assert word timings ±0.25s) is precisely the mechanism the Stripe/R2 seams still lack.
unmade_decisions: What 'required' means and where that list lives as data. It currently exists in three inconsistent places: GitHub's protection API (authoritative), docs/BRANCHING.md (a copy), and scattered ci.yml comments (wrong). Pick one source and test the others against it.

A stated policy that a gate must be able to fail. `|| true`, unguarded pipes, continue-on-error: true, paths-filter skips-as-success, and run_layer0.py's skip-without---require are five distinct mechanisms for the same outcome, each individually justified somewhere, with no rule spanning them — which is why the class recurs under new names.

Whether per-module coverage floors are hand-chosen or auto-ratcheted. The hand-chosen model is exactly why eight high-churn packages (routers/ worker/ billing/ youtube/ chat/ knowledge/ dna/ ingestion/) have none. run_layer0.py --update-baseline already exists and docs/assessment/baselines.json already does this globally.

The lifecycle of a skip. @pytest.mark.quarantine has a documented lifecycle and a hard prohibition on rerun-as-gate (pytest.ini:10-13). @pytest.mark.skip has none, and 70 have accumulated. Either skips get an expiry/tracking convention like quarantine's, or they get deleted.

Frontend coverage: measured or explicitly declined. No `coverage` block in frontend/vite.config.ts and no DECISIONS entry. At 260 source files against 92 test files, 'we deliberately do not measure it because Playwright + structural contract tests carry it' is defensible — it just isn't written down, so nobody can tell it from an omission.

Whether production is a test environment. frontend/playwright.config.prod.ts, e2e/prod/, scripts/live_smoke.py, scripts/drills.py, scripts/clip_audit.py and scripts/eval_efficacy.py all exist and all run only when a human remembers. Continuously-scheduled synthetic journeys against real prod are the highest-value unbuilt mechanism in this domain and are currently neither test nor monitoring.

Whether the global 83% coverage floor should be demoted to a report, leaving diff_cover --fail-under=80 as the actual gate — which is what current practice does and what is already doing the real work here.

Which external seams get real-shape replay. The projection/golden pattern exists for YouTube Data API, Anthropic, and Deepgram; Stripe, R2/boto3 presigning, Voyage, and the YouTube publish path have nothing. Decide the list explicitly rather than adding one per incident.

findings.title: The mutation gate has never executed a single mutant and is structurally incapable of failing (vacuous-green instance #5)
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/mutation.yml:48 (`mutmut run || true`), :52 (`mutmut results | tee` — pipeline exit status is tee's), :53-58 (`{ … } >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` group status is the trailing echo); pyproject.toml:139-160 (`also_copy` omits flags.py, ingestion, chat, improvement, media, notify, analysis, shared_resources.py, verbose.py); routers/review.py:26, routers/clips.py:27, routers/auth.py:18 (`from flags import require_flag`); CI run 32007314899 log: `mutmut.__main__.BadTestExecutionCommandsException`; artifact mutmut_results.txt = 990/990 mutants "not checked"; run 28359402567 (2026-06-29) = 796/796 "not checked"; `gh run list --workflow mutation.yml --limit 8` → 8 × success
findings.failure_scenario: Someone weakens clip_engine/scoring.py's setup-vs-aftermath comparison from `<=` to `<` — literally mutant #86, the one docs/DECISIONS.md:2735 cites as proof the gate works. Every unit test passes, line coverage is unchanged, the weekly mutation job reports success, and nobody learns the tests never asserted on that comparison. Root cause: mutmut removes the repo root from sys.path and runs from ./mutants/, so tests/conftest.py → import main → routers/* → `from flags import require_flag` raises ModuleNotFoundError inside the sandbox; collection fails, mutmut aborts at the stats phase, `|| true` swallows the non-zero exit, and the piped `mutmut results` can never fail either. By contrast llm-e2e-nightly.yml:88-91 and :120-121 correctly use ${PIPESTATUS[0]} — the knowledge is in the repo, the invariant is not.
findings.standard: Mutation testing at scale is diff-scoped and surfaced in review, never a full-repo per-PR gate (Google mutates only changed lines, suppresses uncovered/'arid' lines, shows ~1 mutant per diff to the reviewer). But whatever the cadence, the score is the artifact: a run reporting 'success' must be distinguishable from a run that checked zero mutants. Stryker's incremental mode (since 6.2, ~94% result reuse) is the tooling analogue; mutmut has no incremental mode.
findings.verifier_note: Core fully verified; two corrections. (1) ROOT CAUSE: the first missing module is shared_resources.py, not flags.py — the sandbox import chain dies at conftest.py:37 `from main import app` -> main.py:24 `import event_log` -> event_log.py:38 `from shared_resources import register_aclose` -> ModuleNotFoundError, long before any router reaches `from flags import require_flag`. Fixing flags.py alone would not fix the job; the whole first-party import closure (shared_resources.py, flags.py, verbose.py, analysis/, chat/, improvement/, ingestion/, media/, notify/) must be added to also_copy. (2) SEVERITY: medium, not high. `|| true` is a DELIBERATE, documented choice (DECISIONS.md:2688-2695) so the job can never red-wall a PR, and the job is not in the 8 required contexts — it blocks nothing, so no defect can ship because of it. The real harm is that the project has had zero test-assertion signal on crypto.py / clip_engine/scoring.py / preference/decay.py since the workflow was created (2026-06-29 at the latest), while DECISIONS.md claims a >80% score is being tracked. The correct fix is not to remove `|| true` but to add a hard assertion that the run checked >0 mutants (e.g. `grep -qv 'not checked' mutmut_results.txt || exit 1`, or `EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}` on the results pipeline as llm-e2e-nightly.yml:88-91 and :120-121 already do correctly). This is a legitimate AUDIT_BRIEF section-6 'instance #5' candidate — same shape as instances 3 and 4.

findings.title: Nothing machine-checks which checks are required; `Visual regression` documents itself as gating and is not
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:606-609 comment "GATING since 2026-07-29 (ready-pass W2)"; docs/BRANCHING.md:104-124 applied contexts list omits it; tests/test_ci_config.py has 22 tests over the CI/CD YAML and none about the required-status set

findings.standard: Branch-protection configuration is data and should be version-controlled and asserted against the pipeline definition; a control that describes itself as active while being inert is the canonical 'verification theatre' anti-pattern. findings.title: Three advisory CI jobs are 25/25 green and cost zero to promote; the 92-file frontend suite gates nothing
findings.evidence: ci.yml:437-457 (Frontend), :255-417 (Migration lint Squawk), :606-664 (Visual regression); measured across the last 25 ci.yml runs via gh: Frontend 25/25 success, Migration lint 25/25, Visual regression 25/25; docs/BRANCHING.md:104-124 required contexts
findings.failure_scenario: OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:22 is the template — review/YourCall.tsx:124 hardcoded text-success so 'Error — try again' rendered in success green and the panel closed before awaiting the POST, silently discarding the creator's rating. A vitest test asserting the error branch renders with the error token catches that class, and today that test can go red while the PR still merges. findings.standard: Checks that already run on every PR and pass consistently should be required; leaving them advisory buys no speed and removes all enforcement. Promotion here is a one-line change to the protection contexts and adds zero CI minutes.
findings.verifier_note: Core confirmed (three consistently-green jobs excluded from the required contexts; promotion is a one-line protection change costing zero CI minutes). Three corrections. (1) The cited exemplar does not support the claim: docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md's 2026-08-05 YourCall.tsx row states in bold '**No gate could have caught this:** design-tokens.contract.test.ts only flags *undeclared* token names, and both text-success and text-danger are declared in index.css, so the wrong-but-valid token compiles and ships.' Promoting the Frontend job would not have caught it; the argument is about future enforceability, not this bug. (2) Scope is narrower than stated: `npm run build` is ALREADY gated transitively — Dockerfile:68-71 runs `npm ci` + `npm run build`, and 'Docker build (smoke test)' IS a required context. The genuinely unguarded surface is eslint + the 92 vitest files only. (3) The strongest instance is Visual regression, not Frontend: it is documented in two places as GATING and is not in the required set — that is a follow-through defect, not a policy choice. Severity medium is defensible; the 'standard' citation is weak (DORA 2025 and the Google coverage post say nothing about promoting advisory checks — this is reasonable engineering taste, correctly self-flagged as judgement_call).

findings.title: Nothing reconciles externally-registered endpoints (Stripe webhook, OAuth redirect) with the app's route table
findings.evidence: scripts/doctor.py:400-417 (correctly hardened to probe Stripe through the app's own _STRIPE singleton, closing the transport layer only); grep for `WebhookEndpoint` across the repo returns zero hits; routers/billing.py serves /billing/webhook (exercised at tests/test_billing.py:364 and 8 other sites) while the registered endpoint was /webhooks/stripe

findings.standard: For third-party providers you cannot run Pact verification against, the standard is consumer-side schema/contract validation plus reconciliation of configuration against the served surface. The free read `stripe.WebhookEndpoint.list()` → assert urlparse(url).path resolves in main.app.routes is ~15 lines.

findings.title: `Unit` and `Coverage floor` each execute the entire 3,234-test lane; ~190s of duplicated work per PR
findings.evidence: ci.yml:113-114 (`pytest --tb=short -q`) and ci.yml:239-253 (run_layer0.py --gates coverage,module_coverage,diff_cover, whose gate_coverage runs the same lane under pytest-cov); measured on runs 31908591494/31895047970/31894386424: Unit 197-209s, Coverage 186-191s, on separate runners with separate Redis services and separate dependency installs
findings.failure_scenario: Not a correctness bug — a budget one. ~3.5 runner-minutes per PR are spent re-running tests that just ran, on a solo-maintainer budget, while the 260-file frontend has no coverage measurement at all (no `coverage` block in frontend/vite.config.ts) and the prod-journey specs in e2e/prod/ run never. The unique signal of the second job is three threshold comparisons over an XML file.
findings.standard: Run the suite once under coverage and publish the artifact to the gate step; Google's guidance treats the global percentage as a report and diff coverage on changed lines as the gate (diff_cover --fail-under in the 70-80 band, already at 80 here).
findings.verifier_note: The facts are right and the harm is imaginary. Verified: ci.yml:114 runs `pytest --tb=short -q`, and run_layer0.py:198-208 (gate_coverage) re-runs `pytest -q --no-header --cov . --cov-report xml:...`, so the lane does execute twice. Durations from the three cited runs are accurate (Unit 203s/197s/209s, Coverage 189s/191s/186s). But the finding's entire load-bearing claim is 'a budget one... ~3.5 runner-minutes per PR on a solo-maintainer budget' — and `gh repo view` returns {"isPrivate":false,"visibility":"PUBLIC"}. GitHub Actions on standard runners is free and unmetered for public repositories, and docs/BRANCHING.md:67-69 explicitly notes the repo was made public. The cost is $0. Nor is there a wall-clock cost: the two jobs start at the same timestamp on separate runners and Coverage finishes FIRST in two of the three sampled runs, so it is never on the critical path. The jobs are also not duplicates — the Unit job additionally runs `pytest --collect-only -q` as a dependency-drift import smoke (ci.yml:110-114) and the Issue-478 render_env lane with real ffmpeg + mediapipe + the pinned BlazeFace model, none of which the Coverage job runs. Finally, consolidating them is actively hazardous here: ci.yml:243-252 documents that the previous shape, where coverage artifacts were shared across invocations, caused module_coverage and diff_cover to report 'skipped' with exit 0 on every PR from 2026-06-23 to 2026-08-12 — the exact 7-week vacuous-gate outage recorded as instance #3 in AUDIT_BRIEF section 6. Issue 479 deliberately separated concerns to fix that. Two independent pytest invocations also mean a crash in the coverage tracer still leaves live test signal. The supporting asides are also loose: `e2e/prod` does not exist at repo root (it is frontend/e2e/prod, referenced by npm scripts test:prod:auth — a manual auth-capture helper, not an unrun spec suite). No real cost, no real risk, and the proposed remedy reintroduces a defect the project just spent an issue removing.

findings.title: ~4,400 lines of tests aimed at deleted code or named by issue number, including the largest file in tests/
findings.evidence: tests/test_static.py — 1,861 lines, largest file in tests/, 80 test functions, 34 @pytest.mark.skip with reasons of the form "Issue 226: static/index.html retired — React SPA is canonical"; 8 × tests/test_issue_*.py totalling 2,605 lines (test_issue_104, _105_worker_idempotency, _110, _113, _125, _126, _139, _88_filter_parity)
