The guard exists and is unfindable. Separately, test_static.py sits at the top of any 'what does this project test?' reading while testing a subsystem that was deleted.
findings.standard: Pareto testing (the project's own global CLAUDE.md rule): ~20% of tests should cover ~80% of value; skips should be deleted rather than accumulated, and test files should be named for the behaviour they protect. The skip count is already known (AUDIT_KNOWN_ISSUES §C4) — the new signal is the size ranking and the issue-numbered file family.
findings.verifier_note: Narrow to what is actually true. (a) DEAD MASS: 34 skipped functions in tests/test_static.py (Issue-226 residue) plus 8 skips across the issue-numbered files should be deleted — order of a few hundred lines, not 4,400. This is already a conceded item (AUDIT_BRIEF section 5, AUDIT_KNOWN_ISSUES C4), so it is a confirmation, not new signal. (b) NEW SIGNAL, and it is a rename not a delete: the eight tests/test_issue_*.py files hold 77 LIVE tests named for when they were written rather than what they protect, and tests/test_static.py's name no longer describes a file that is now largely the compliance/security-header/legal-copy suite. Recommend renaming/splitting (e.g. test_static.py -> test_security_headers.py + test_legal_pages.py; test_issue_110.py -> test_rate_limit_decorators.py), explicitly NOT deleting. (c) Separately worth promoting: AUDIT_KNOWN_ISSUES C4 flags two skips in tests/test_notifications.py:636 and tests/test_notifications_triggers.py:652 marked 'needs real Postgres' when an integration lane with live PG exists — those should become @pytest.mark.integration and actually run, which is higher value than any of the above. Severity low is correct.

domains.verdict_headline: The pipeline's shape is better than the project's reputation: the required set, runner trust boundary (Issue 360), data-bearing staging gate, and the strict+linear+no-push-trigger combination are all correct and several are above standard for this scale. The failures are not architectural — three gates report success while doing nothing (dead CalVer release automation, a prod smoke that skips itself, a local gate that prints "passed" after skipping everything), which is the repo's named #1 failure class showing up in its own delivery tooling. The single highest-value change is also free: three of the four advisory checks already run on every PR and finish 1.5–3.5 minutes before the required set closes, so promoting them to required costs zero PR latency.
strengths: The no-`push: [main]` trigger is genuinely sound, not the hole it looks like: with `strict: true` plus `required_linear_history` forcing squash/rebase, the tree landing on main is byte-identical to the PR head the 8 checks ran against. Re-running ~12 jobs post-merge would burn minutes for zero new signal. Do not add it. (ci.yml:27-33, docs/BRANCHING.md:100-127)

The runner trust boundary (Issue 360, DECISIONS.md:12558) is exactly right and better than most small teams manage — PR-triggered code never touches the self-hosted runner that has docker-group membership and read access to /opt/autoclip/.env. ci.yml:11-25 states the threat model explicitly and instructs the future maintainer 'if the spending limit fast-fails PR CI, fix billing; do NOT move these jobs back.'
`permissions: contents: read` at workflow level with per-job escalation (ci.yml:53-54) — current GitHub-hardening standard, and rare in a repo this young.

tests/test_ci_config.py (22 tests asserting properties of the CI/CD YAML itself) is above standard. It is the mechanism that converts 'we learned X about our pipeline' into 'X cannot regress' — and it is the correct home for the fixes to findings 1 and 2.

The data-bearing staging gate (deploy.yml:31-147) is the strongest thing in the pipeline and above standard for this scale: the exact sha- image under test deployed against a persistent staging_postgres_data volume with an in-container `alembic current == heads` assertion. CI's fresh-DB bootstrap structurally cannot catch data-dependent migration failures; this can.

Auto-rollback that still exits 1 (deploy.yml:339) — a rollback is a safety net, not a success signal — with `docker image prune` correctly moved to after a green smoke so a failed deploy cannot delete its own rollback target.
unmade_decisions: What 'release identity' means for this product — humans (support/rollback), machines (Sentry release grouping), or customers. Issue 297 answered 'which scheme' without answering 'who reads it', which is why nobody noticed it went inert.

A stated principle for what makes a check required. The 8-vs-4 split is an accretion, not a rule; without something like 'a check is required if its failure would reach production undetected', Migration lint sitting advisory while Docker build blocks is indistinguishable from an oversight.
What replaces code review. DECISIONS.md records why there is no required review; it records nothing about a substitute, in a repo where CI catches <10% of defects and 0 of the SEV1s.
Whether ci_local.sh is a gate or an advisory convenience. It is documented as a gate (ci.yml:11-25 calls it 'Layer 1') and behaves as an advisory. Pick one and encode it in the exit contract.
Dependency-update cadence. The implicit current answer — 'the required pip-audit check red-walls everything until you fix it by hand' — is a policy nobody chose.
An expiry convention for PIP_AUDIT_IGNORES. Five suppressions carry 're-evaluate when the venv is rebuilt' with no owner and no date; a suppression without an expiry is a permanent hole.

Whether deploy.yml / docker-publish.yml need a concurrency group, or whether single-self-hosted-runner FIFO serialization is the accepted mechanism. Currently neither workflow declares one and the reasoning is nowhere.

What the stale CI/deploy rows in OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md are for — :42 is factually obsolete (fixed by Issue 360) yet still marked Open, and :81 (LLM E2E Nightly red on main) has been open since 2026-07-02. The visual-regression comment/config contradiction survived a month partly because that log is no longer read.

findings.title: CalVer release automation has been a silent no-op for 636 commits; /health reports version "dev" in production
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:85-106 (tag+release step, every failure swallowed by `|| echo`); pyproject.toml:6 (`version = "2026.6.0"`, unchanged since June); main.py:83-85 (importlib.metadata fallback to "dev"); main.py:128 (hardcoded FastAPI version="0.1.0"); Dockerfile runtime stage (`COPY . .` — project is never pip-installed); docs/DECISIONS.md:11659 (Issue 297)
findings.failure_scenario: Verified today: `git ls-remote --tags origin` returns exactly one tag (v2026.6.0 @ 01afa46, 2026-06-23); `git rev-list --count v2026.6.0..origin/main` = 636; `gh release list` is EMPTY (so `gh release create` has never once succeeded and the `release: published` trigger has never fired — no image has ever carried a CalVer tag); `curl https://autoclip.studio/health` returns {"version":"dev"}. Because the Dockerfile never installs the project as a package, importlib.metadata.version("creatorclip") always raises PackageNotFoundError, so /health has never reported a real version in any environment. Operational consequence: a degraded deploy at 02:00 — the operator hits /health (the documented 'what version is live' touchpoint, main.py:564-566) and gets "dev"; the human-readable rollback target the decision promised resolves to a June build 636 commits stale; the only true identity is the GHCR digest, recoverable only by SSH-ing to the VM. Zero tests reference __version__ or importlib.metadata anywhere in tests/, including tests/test_ci_config.py which pins every other property of this pipeline.
findings.standard: Both accepted 2026 release shapes (semantic-release: tag on every qualifying push; release-please: tag on merging a Release PR) share one non-negotiable — every shipping push produces a distinct, immutable identifier and the running artifact can state its own identity. release-please is now the more commonly recommended default specifically because it removes the manual version-bump step, which is exactly the step that killed this implementation.
findings.verifier_note: Severity: MEDIUM (not high). Accurate statement: the Issue-297 CalVer layer has been a no-op since it shipped — one tag (v2026.6.0, 636 commits stale), zero GitHub Releases, so the `release: published` trigger and the `type=semver` metadata rule have never fired and no image has ever carried a CalVer tag. Independently, `/health` reports `"version":"dev"` in every environment because the Dockerfile never pip-installs the project, so `importlib.metadata.version("creatorclip")` always raises. Both are silent because docker-publish.yml:98-106 swallows every failure with `|| echo`. DROP the claim that image identity is SSH-only: the running commit SHA is publicly visible as `?v=sha-<full-sha>` on every served HTML page (verified live = HEAD 1def133), and images already carry an immutable `sha-<commit>` tag. The real defect is (1) the loss of the human-readable rollback label the decision promised, (2) `/health` making a false-but-plausible version statement, and (3) an automation that cannot report its own failure. Cheapest honest fixes: drop `|| echo` on `gh release create` (or `|| exit 1`), and report `{"version": <literal from pyproject or build arg>, "sha": settings.IMAGE_SHA}` from /health instead of relying on importlib.metadata over a non-installed package.

findings.title: Prod deploy's critical-journey smoke silently downgrades to a warning when CC_JWT_SECRET is unset — the staging gate 230 lines above it cannot
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/deploy.yml:365-370 (`if [ -z "${CC_JWT_SECRET:-}" ]; then echo "WARNING: … skipping critical journey smoke."`); deploy.yml:318 (secret sourced from GitHub `secrets.CC_JWT_SECRET`); contrast deploy.yml:136 (staging sources it in-container: `sh -c 'CC_JWT_SECRET="$JWT_SECRET_KEY" python scripts/llm_harness.py --flow core'`); docs/assessment/modules/deploy_ci.md:156 lists CC_JWT_SECRET as an undocumented .env.example gap
findings.failure_scenario: CC_JWT_SECRET is unset or rotated without re-syncing (nothing in the repo establishes it is set). Every prod deploy then validates exactly one thing: /health returns status:ok five times — the same check that stayed green through the 10-week Stripe outage, the 7-week catalog-sync outage and the 9-day silent-prod incident. A deploy that breaks auth_me, videos_list, dna, insights, billing_balance or the videos envelope shape passes; auto-rollback (Issue 271/295) is armed on liveness only; `docker image prune -f` then runs and deletes the rollback target; the run reports green. Same defect class as OFF_COURSE_BUGS:148 ('a pre-flight doctor that green-lights a subsystem it does not actually exercise is worse than no check'), sitting on the last gate before prod declares itself healthy. Fix is one line — mirror the staging invocation, or `exit 1` instead of `echo WARNING`.
findings.standard: A deploy-verification gate must fail closed on missing configuration; 'could not run' must never share an outcome with 'ran and passed'. Decide the failure mode explicitly — fail closed for security/verification gates, fail open only for advisory ones.
findings.verifier_note: Severity: MEDIUM (not high). Strengthen the evidence, narrow the scope. Evidence upgrade: CC_JWT_SECRET is provably absent from the repository's GitHub secrets (`gh secret list`) and CC_CREATOR_ID absent from variables (`gh variable list`), so deploy.yml:365-370 has taken the WARNING branch on every prod deploy since Issue 295 shipped — the prod critical-journey smoke has never run once, while all eight recent deploy runs report success. Scope correction: this does NOT mean code regressions in auth_me/videos_list/dna/insights/billing_balance/videos_envelope ship unverified — deploy-staging (a hard `needs:` dependency) runs the identical `llm_harness --flow core` against a data-bearing staging DB with the same image and exits 1 on failure. The genuinely unguarded set is prod-only failure modes: /opt/autoclip/.env drift, prod DB state, live Stripe/R2/CORS config, and the skip_staging break-glass path — precisely the class that produced the 10-week Stripe and silent-prod incidents. Auto-rollback remaining armed on liveness only, and `docker image prune -f` then removing the rollback target, are both confirmed. Fix: either `exit 1` instead of `echo WARNING`, or mirror the staging invocation (`app sh -c 'CC_JWT_SECRET="$JWT_SECRET_KEY" python3 scripts/llm_harness.py --flow core'`) so it needs no GitHub secret at all — the latter is strictly better since it also removes the rotation-desync failure mode.

findings.title: Three of the four advisory gates cost zero PR latency to make required; visual regression already claims in-file to be gating
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:255-417 (migration-lint), :437-457 (frontend), :606-664 (visual, comment at :606-609 says "GATING since 2026-07-29"); docs/BRANCHING.md:100-127 (required list — none of the three appear); frontend/package.json:10 (`"test": "vitest run"`, default reporter); docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:133,147,157 (same vitest flake, name never captured); :42 (stale — fixed by Issue 360)
findings.failure_scenario: Measured across 4 consecutive real CI runs (gh run view 31908591494 / 31895047970 / 31894386424 / 31893721420): all 12 jobs start within 3s of each other; critical path is Integration tests at 3m34s–4m29s; Migration lint 20–25s, Visual regression 43–57s, Frontend 1m47s–1m49s — all finish 2–3.5 minutes BEFORE the gate closes. Promoting them adds 0 seconds to time-to-merge. Concrete failure today: a migration adding `ALTER TABLE clips … SET NOT NULL` merges with Squawk red and takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the largest table during prod deploy — Squawk plus the downgrade round-trip is the ONLY automated protection on the path that already produced the silent-no-op-migration incident (ISSUES_LOG:556) and the invalid `UPDATE … LIMIT` backfill snippet (OFF_COURSE_BUGS:142). Separately, ci.yml:606-609 asserting the visual job is 'GATING since 2026-07-29' while it is absent from the required contexts means the belief 'visual regressions are gated' is simply false. Caveat on Frontend: capture the cold-run vitest flake first by adding `--reporter=verbose` (a `test:ci` script) — it has been logged three times with the failing test name never recorded.
findings.standard: Strict required checks improve safety but amplify flakiness pain — fix test determinism before tightening rules. Mutation testing correctly stays non-gating (the objection is semantic, not temporal: a mutation score over 3 files is a trend metric, and gating it either red-walls unrelated PRs or gets ratcheted to meaninglessness).
findings.verifier_note: Severity: MEDIUM (not high). Accurate statement: migration-lint, frontend and visual regression run unconditionally on every PR (no job-level `if:`, no `continue-on-error` — only detect-flakes has that), always report a real conclusion, and finish 2-3.5 minutes before the critical-path Integration job, yet none appear in the 8 required contexts in docs/BRANCHING.md:100-127. Promoting all three costs zero PR latency. The sharpest sub-finding is the config/doc contradiction: ci.yml:605-609 states the visual job has been 'GATING since 2026-07-29' when branch protection has never required it. REMOVE the claim that Squawk is the automated guard for the silent-no-op-migration incident — that was an alembic/env.py non-committing-transaction bug (ISSUE-2026-06-24-02) which neither Squawk nor the schema round-trip would catch; argue migration-lint on its own merits (unsafe DDL locks, irreversible downgrades). Mitigating context the finding omits: all three already show red in the PR checks UI, and the maintainer reviews every PR, so this is defence-in-depth against a tired-merge, not an unguarded path. Keep the Frontend caveat: capture the recurring vitest flake (add a `test:ci` script with `--reporter=verbose`) before promoting that one. Also flag that docs/AUDIT_KNOWN_ISSUES.md:99 ('Playwright and visual fail on the self-hosted runner, 0 tests run') is stale — both now pass on ubuntu-latest.

findings.title: ci_local.sh prints "Local CI passed." and exits 0 after skipping every gate it was asked to run
findings.evidence: scripts/ci_local.sh:73,82,93,112,113,121,130 (six skip-and-continue paths: ruff/python3/pytest missing, Redis down, node_modules absent); :156 (skipped count printed) vs :162 (`Local CI passed.` + exit 0); :95 (`run_layer0.py --gates mypy,bandit` with NO `--require` — same shape that made coverage gates no-op for 7 weeks, Issue 479); .githooks/pre-push:25 (execs the script, inherits its exit code)
findings.failure_scenario: Developer box with Redis not running and frontend/node_modules never installed (the maintainer's own documented environment): pytest skipped, coverage skipped, the entire frontend block skipped. Two of six gates actually ran. `git push` succeeds and the terminal prints 'Local CI passed.' in green. Layer 1 of the documented two-layer CI model reports verified having checked ~15% of what it names — the same shape as ci.yml:28-31's premise being false when the pre-push hook was not installed at all. Additionally, a stale .venv that breaks mypy produces a green local static gate because line 95 omits --require.
findings.standard: Pass and could-not-run must not share an exit code. Canonical precedent: kselftest reserves exit 4 for 'skipped', distinct from 0 for 'passed'; general CI-script guidance is to decide the failure mode explicitly and fail closed for verification gates. Fix: never print 'passed' when SKIPPED is non-empty; classify core (pytest, static) vs best-effort gates and exit non-zero on a skipped core gate; add `--require mypy,bandit` to line 95. Keep --no-verify and CI_LOCAL_SKIP — a bypass the developer chooses is honest; one that happens by itself and reports success is not.
findings.verifier_note:
The line citations all resolve (73, 82, 93, 112, 113, 121, 130, 95, 156, 162; the pre-push exec is at line 24, not 25). But the finding dies on three independent grounds.

(1) The failure premise is factually false about the environment it names. It asserts 'a developer box with Redis not running and frontend/node_modules never installed (the maintainer's own documented environment)'. On this box: `redis-cli ping` -> PONG; `frontend/node_modules` exists; `.venv/bin/ruff`, `.venv/bin/mypy`, `.venv/bin/pytest` all present (and ci_local.sh:41 PATH-prefixes .venv/bin); `git config core.hooksPath` -> .githooks. The '2 of 6 gates ran, ~15% checked' scenario is constructed, not observed. The referenced memory note says Docker is unavailable and tests run with python3.12 + brew redis — i.e. Redis IS the documented local setup, the opposite of the premise.

(2) It rediscovers an explicitly documented decision without engaging its reasoning. ci_local.sh:24 states the contract in the header: 'Exit 1 if any RUN gate fails; skips (absent tool/service, no changed files) are OK.' Lines 9-14 give the rationale: the repo carries pre-existing gate debt, and 'blocking on that would force --no-verify on every push' — i.e. failing closed here was tried and defeats the gate entirely. Lines 97-109 record the concrete regression from being stricter (a stale `-m` filter re-selected render_env/llm_live/transcription_live lanes, erroring for everyone and forcing --no-verify on every push; Issue 479). The success message at :162 is not the bare 'Local CI passed' the finding quotes — it reads 'Local CI passed. Docker-only gates (integration, eval, playwright) run on the self-hosted runner', explicitly scoping its own claim. Per the audit brief's own instruction, arguing this requires engaging the stated tradeoff, which the finding does not do.

(3) The consequence does not exist. Layer 1 is non-authoritative by design. main is branch-protected with 8 required contexts and enforce_admins:true (docs/BRANCHING.md, commit 8c4d286), and ci.yml:28-31 documents that the `push` trigger is deliberately omitted because every change reaches main via a PR that runs the full suite. A vacuously-green pre-push hook cannot put one unverified line into main — the worst case is a wasted CI round-trip. Contrast the three real section-6 instances (catalog sync, Stripe, coverage floors), where the vacuous green was the ONLY signal and something shipped broken. Nothing ships on ci_local.sh's word.

Residual nit that does not rescue the finding: line 95 omits `--require`, so a gate whose tool is uninstalled returns 'skipped' and the aggregator prints 'All runnable gates passed'. But gate_mypy (run_layer0.py:167-172) returns 'skipped' ONLY when `_have("mypy")` is false — a 'stale .venv that breaks mypy' does not produce that state, so the finding's specific failure sentence is wrong. And the identical omission exists in the authoritative ci.yml static-gates job (`--gates ruff,mypy,bandit,pip_audit,freshness`, no `--require`), which is where it would actually matter and which the finding never mentions. The Issue-479 analogy is also mis-drawn: that was an XML-deletion ordering bug between two invocations; `--require` was the defence added afterwards, not the thing that broke.

findings.title: No required review is the right call, but nothing was put in its place in a repo where CI catches under 10% of defects and zero of the SEV1s
findings.evidence: docs/BRANCHING.md:129-131 (`required_pull_request_reviews: null` — correct: a solo maintainer cannot self-approve); .github/ contains only workflows/ (no PR template, no CODEOWNERS, no AI-review workflow); 00-groundtruth/snag-taxonomy.md §B (every SEV1/BLOCKER caught at production or by a deliberate audit, none by CI; CI contributes ~9% of finds); docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:22 ('No gate could have caught this')
findings.failure_scenario: An AI-generated PR renders a failure string in `text-success` (OFF_COURSE_BUGS:22 — the rating was silently discarded and the error rendered in success green), or adds a test whose assertion is `all([])` (:154). Ruff, mypy, bandit, coverage, integration and Playwright all pass — none read for intent. It merges, auto-deploys, and is found weeks later by the owner looking at a screenshot. That is the modal history of this repo: findings arrive in bursts of 27 from paid audits, not from the pipeline. Recommendation (judgement call): add anthropics/claude-code-action as a PR job scoped to the two classes gates cannot catch (vacuous assertions; user-facing string styling contradicting its content), and keep it NON-BLOCKING — making an LLM reviewer a required check in this specific repo would create a new Class-1 gate that can pass by not looking. Pair with a 3-line self-review checklist in a PR template. Explicitly do NOT add a merge queue: at ~2-4 merges/day, `strict: true` already buys the only property a queue provides.
findings.standard: DORA 2025 found AI raises authoring throughput without raising review capacity, making review the dominant bottleneck, and names shifting automation into the author/PR phase as the countermeasure. GitHub's own 'prevent self-review' setting encodes that a lone self-approver is not a control. Over 1.3M repos now run an AI code-review integration; the guidance is that it is advisory until placed in the required-status list — and that a solo maintainer should be wary of making the human slot agent-on-agent.

findings.title: pip-audit is a required check pinned at a zero baseline with no automated dependency-update path and no expiry on suppressions
findings.evidence: .claude/skills/production-assessment/scripts/run_layer0.py:268-281 (gate_pip_audit → metric pip_audit_vulns, compare max) vs docs/assessment/baselines.json (pip_audit_vulns 0); .github/workflows/ci.yml:419-435 (inside the required `Types + SAST + deps` check); run_layer0.py:227-265 (PIP_AUDIT_IGNORES — 5+ hand-maintained suppressions with 're-evaluate when the venv is rebuilt' and no date); no .github/dependabot.yml, no renovate.json, no CODEOWNERS
findings.failure_scenario: A CVE is published overnight against a transitive dependency. The next morning every open PR — including an unrelated production hotfix — fails a required check that has nothing to do with the change. There is no bot PR waiting with the bump: requirements.txt is hand-pinned with ==, so the maintainer must diagnose, find a compatible version and re-pin by hand before anything can merge, during an incident. The existing coping mechanism is a suppression list with no expiry dates and no scheduled review, so the pressure is toward permanently widening the hole rather than fixing it.
findings.standard: Automated dependency updates (Dependabot/Renovate) with GROUPED weekly PRs are the standard companion to a zero-tolerance vulnerability gate; grouping is specifically what makes it tolerable for a solo maintainer (one PR a week, not fifteen). Suppressions carry an owner and an expiry.

domains.verdict_headline: The diagnostic half of this process is above industry standard — "wrong hypotheses ruled out" logs, adversarial verifier subagents, and a decision log that retracts its own diagnoses. The corrective half is missing: nine recurring gotchas each have a correct structural fix written down in the row that reported them, and none of the nine was built, because the entire Claude Code hook surface is unused locally (the only hook exits 0 unless CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true). The four-phase issue loop is not the churn source; Phase 4 being a ~30-item human checklist is.
strengths: ~/.claude/ISSUES_LOG.md's 'Wrong hypotheses (ruled out -- don't repeat these)' section on all 36 entries. Recording refuted branches is the information that actually prevents the next investigation, and almost no postmortem practice does it. Protect this from any pruning.

Adversarial verifier subagents in the 2026-08-12 audit -- chartered to kill each finding, refuted 2 outright and materially corrected 10 (CLIPPING_INTEGRITY_2026-08-12.md:97-99). This is Anthropic's now-documented 'adversarial review step', arrived at independently.
DECISIONS.md:12884 retracts a prior diagnosis alongside its correction rather than quietly overwriting it -- preserving a wrong diagnosis next to the right one is rare and correct.

tests/test_ci_config.py -- 22 tests asserting properties of the CI/CD YAML itself (deploy runs self-hosted, pre-migration dump precedes alembic, staging sha-pinned never :latest, eval commit status targets PR head sha). When this repo builds a mechanism it builds a very good one; the gap is frequency, not capability.

The eval anti-hollowing ratchet (SCENARIO_FLOOR + skip-marker regex scan, with ratchet history in a comment above the constant) -- a working closing-pressure device already in the repo, and the exact template the OFF_COURSE_BUGS log needs.

docs/AUDIT_BRIEF.md sections 4 and 5 -- warning an external reviewer that `grep TODO` will mislead them, and listing seven things that look like smells and are recorded decisions. An unusually honest and effective orientation artifact.
unmade_decisions: What belongs in CLAUDE.md vs a skill vs a hook vs a test -- no DECISIONS.md entry addresses the project's own agent-instruction architecture, which is why everything defaulted into CLAUDE.md.

A conversion policy stating when prose must become mechanism. Proposed rule: convert when (a) the class has been logged twice, (b) the knowledge must be applied before the failure is observable, (c) the prose is mirrored by a machine, or (d) a script can check it in under a second.
A docs/ size budget and pruning cadence. There is an append path and no forget path; 2026 agent-memory work names forgetting as the most underrated operation.
The ADR format itself -- DECISIONS.md's shape accreted and was never decided. One paragraph choosing MADR-lite (one file per decision, Status field, Superseded-by link) would settle it.
The promote-or-close rule for OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md: how long may a row stay open, and what is the legal way to close one without fixing it.
Whether Phase 2 approval is per-issue or per-wave. Practice has already answered (wave-scope entries in DECISIONS.md); the written process was never updated.
A Phase 4 admissibility rule -- 'a checklist item a script can check must be a script, or be deleted.' This alone would convert roughly eight of the thirty items.

Single-authority rule for project state: which file owns issue status and the next free issue number, and which files may only cite it. Currently issues.md, PROJECT_STATE.md and LEFT_OFF.md all claim it and disagree.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md:120 instructs the exact interpreter that produces phantom results
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:120 (`python3 .claude/skills/production-assessment/scripts/run_layer0.py`); `grep -n venv CLAUDE.md` returns nothing; the rule lives only at LEFT_OFF.md:199; incident at docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:156
findings.failure_scenario: A fresh session follows the Phase 4 checklist literally -> system python3 (fastapi 0.115.4 vs pinned 0.137.1) -> mypy aborts with a vacuous 'ok 0', pip-audit invents ~77 phantom CVEs, four tests fail spuriously. Per OFF_COURSE_BUGS:156 those phantoms were filed as real defect reports and later retracted. Has occurred twice (LEFT_OFF.md:199: 'burned two consecutive sessions... bit again on 2026-08-15').
findings.standard: Anthropic's current Claude Code best-practices page: CLAUDE.md instructions are advisory, hooks are deterministic; 'Use hooks for actions that must happen every time with zero exceptions.' Environment quirks belong in CLAUDE.md but enforcement belongs in a hook or a self-guarding script.
findings.verifier_note: Severity: MEDIUM, not high. Accurate statement: CLAUDE.md:120 — the Phase-4 automated-gate line, the single most-followed instruction in the file — names the interpreter that produces vacuous and phantom Layer-0 results, and CLAUDE.md contains no mention of `.venv` anywhere. The `.venv` rule lives only in LEFT_OFF.md:199 (a file CLAUDE.md's own Read Order does not list) and AUDIT_BRIEF.md §2. run_layer0.py does not self-guard: it binds tools to `sys.executable` and counts mypy errors by grepping for ': error:', so an aborted mypy reports `ok 0`. Blast radius is bounded to the in-session window: `.githooks/pre-push` prefixes PATH with `.venv/bin` and branch protection (8 required checks, enforce_admins:true) means nothing reaches prod on a phantom result. Realized cost across two incidents: retracted defect reports and ~2 sessions. The cheap fixes are (a) change :120 to `.venv/bin/python` or `scripts/ci_local.sh`, and (b) make run_layer0.py fail loudly when a configured mypy plugin cannot load — which OFF_COURSE_BUGS:156 already recommends and nobody built.

findings.title: The mandated session Read Order is ~23,000 lines and is therefore ignored
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:31-42 lists six files required 'before writing a single line of code'; sizes: SOT.md 705 + PROJECT_STATE.md 4,440 + issues.md 4,550 + DECISIONS.md 13,018 + COMPLIANCE.md + CLIPPING_PRINCIPLES.md
findings.failure_scenario: An unsatisfiable mandate is silently dropped every session; once one CLAUDE.md rule is routinely ignored the file's authority degrades uniformly, which is why the wrong interpreter at :120, the dead 'static/' claim at :55 and the wrong WINDOW_S citation at :236 all survived unchallenged. The agent then works from memory -- the exact failure the project's One Rule exists to prevent.
findings.standard: Anthropic: 'Keep it concise. For each line ask: would removing this cause Claude to make mistakes? If not, cut it. Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions.' The exclude-list explicitly names 'information that changes frequently'. 2026 agent-memory practice: progressive disclosure via skills, not monolithic docs.
findings.verifier_note: Severity: LOW-MEDIUM, not high, and the framing should be 'the written rule does not describe the practice' rather than 'the mandate is dropped so the file loses authority'. Accurate statement: CLAUDE.md:31-42 mandates reading ~23,200 lines before any code, which no session can do; the actual working method is targeted grep (documented in the project's own AUDIT_BRIEF.md §4) plus LEFT_OFF.md as a compressed handoff. Anthropic's guidance points at exactly that resolution — 'For domain knowledge or workflows that are only relevant sometimes, use skills instead' — so the fix is to replace 'read these files in order' with 'grep these files by topic; the index is X', not to shrink CLAUDE.md (298 lines is fine). Drop the causal claim entirely: the stale interpreter at :120, the incomplete Project Structure list at :51-55, and the wrong WINDOW_S path at :236 are caused by the absence of a doc-citation test (already identified at OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:158 and folded into Issue 497's acceptance criteria), not by Read Order non-compliance. Also: ':55 dead static/ claim' is false — static/ is live (tos/privacy/accessibility/landing + tokens + fonts); the line is merely incomplete for omitting frontend/.

findings.title: Stale CLAUDE.md prose is a machine input and already seeded a real defect (Issue 497)
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:51-53 omits billing/, chat/, analysis/, notify/, media/; CLAUDE.md:55 'Frontend assets in static/' contradicts CLAUDE.md:227; CLAUDE.md:236 cites clip_engine/window.py for WINDOW_S which is at clip_engine/candidates.py:22; docs/issues.md:4498 (Issue 497) names the stale list as root cause of run_layer0.py::_CANDIDATE_SOURCES gaps
findings.failure_scenario: run_layer0.py mirrors the CLAUDE.md module list, so mypy has never type-checked 4,093 lines and bandit has never scanned 8,277 -- including crypto.py, auth.py, redact.py, api_key.py, flags.py -- while baselines.json reports bandit_high 0 / bandit_medium 0. The next package added to the tree (as chat/ was, where two July SEV2s landed) silently falls outside both gates and nothing detects it.
findings.standard: Docs-as-tests: any doc a machine mirrors is a schema and needs a parity assertion; documentation linting and reference-resolution checks run in CI are standard 2026 practice (Fern, lychee, GitLab docs CI).
findings.verifier_note: Nothing to report as a new finding. Everything load-bearing is Issue 497 (docs/issues.md:4498), disclosed at docs/AUDIT_KNOWN_ISSUES.md §A1 and §H and at docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:158, with the parity-assertion remedy already written as its stated load-bearing acceptance criterion and the fix deliberately withheld pending this review. If anything is worth adding it is one sentence, not a finding: Issue 497's structural-guard AC should be widened from `_sources()` coverage to a general docs-citation test (extract `path` and `path:line` references from CLAUDE.md and docs/*.md, assert each resolves, and for `NAME = value` claims assert the symbol is defined in the cited file) — which OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:158 already proposes verbatim and asks to fold into 497. Strike the `media/` claim (zero .py files, not a package) and the claim that `_CANDIDATE_SOURCES` mirrors CLAUDE.md (it already includes `billing`, which CLAUDE.md omits).

findings.title: The correct structural fix is identified and then not built -- nine documented times
findings.evidence: OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:147 asks for reporter:['verbose'] but frontend/package.json still has "test": "vitest run" (third recurrence at :157); OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:37 status column literally reads 'engines pin open' and frontend/package.json engines is None; the two .nvmrc files disagree (/.nvmrc=22.17.1 vs frontend/.nvmrc=22, ci_local.sh:49 reads only root); OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:157 asks ci_local.sh to print --randomly-seed and preserve lastfailed -- grep finds neither in scripts/ci_local.sh
findings.failure_scenario: The fourth vitest cold-run flake lands in a future session. The failing test name is still not captured, because the capture flag (--reporter=verbose) must be added BEFORE the first run and can only be remembered by someone who already knows the failure is coming. Another session pays ~1 hour and the row gets a fourth entry recommending the same fix. Three sessions have already been spent this way.
findings.standard: Hierarchy of controls applied to postmortem action items: administrative controls (docs, checklists, 'remember to') are second-weakest and rely on human recall at the moment of exposure; engineering controls (defaults, hard failures) are the effective class. Teams closing action items within 30 days measurably reduce recurrence.
findings.verifier_note: Severity: LOW-MEDIUM, not high. Accurate statement: at least four structural remediations recorded in docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md's remediation column remain unbuilt on this tree — (a) :147's `reporter: ['verbose']` in frontend/vite.config.ts (file has `restoreMocks: true` at :66, no reporter key; package.json test script is still bare `vitest run`); (b) :37's `engines` pin in frontend/package.json (absent; the tracking column literally says 'engines pin open'); (c) :157's `--randomly-seed` echo and `.pytest_cache/v/cache/lastfailed` preservation in scripts/ci_local.sh (neither string appears); (d) :157's reconciliation of the `failed: 0` vs `LOCAL CI FAILED` disagreement. Drop 'nine documented times' — four are evidenced. Drop the '.nvmrc files disagree' item: root 22.17.1, frontend 22 and CI 'node-version: 22' all resolve to 22.x, and the documented breakage is node 26. The vitest cold-run flake has two recurrences (:133, :147), not three; :157 is a distinct pytest-randomly ordering flake sharing only the 'failing identity not self-recording' meta-pattern. The honest failure scenario is the next cold vitest run flaking with the name again uncaptured, costing a fourth session ~1 hour — not a product defect.

findings.title: The entire Claude Code hook surface is unused locally -- every project rule is advisory
findings.evidence: .claude/settings.json registers only SessionStart; .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:12 exits 0 unless CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true; no PreToolUse, PostToolUse or Stop hook exists; no .claude/workflows/ (the memory index claims an issue-wave.js harness that is not present)
findings.failure_scenario: With no Stop hook nothing can refuse to end a turn on a red suite -- OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:152 records 'W4 was merged while red -- process failure noted'. With no PreToolUse hook nothing can refuse a bare `python3` -- producing the phantom-defect incident at :156. Every rule this project has is enforceable only by recall, and the corpus shows each has been violated at least once.
findings.standard: Anthropic: 'Use hooks for actions that must happen every time with zero exceptions... Unlike CLAUDE.md instructions which are advisory, hooks are deterministic and guarantee the action happens.' Plus the documented Stop-hook-as-deterministic-gate and adversarial-review-subagent rungs.
findings.verifier_note: Severity: LOW, not high, and rescope from 'every project rule is advisory' to 'nothing gates the in-session window'. Accurate statement: the Claude Code hook surface is unused locally — .claude/settings.json registers only SessionStart, and .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:12 no-ops unless CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true, so no PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop hook exists; .claude/workflows and issue-wave.js do not exist despite the memory index claiming them. But the project does have deterministic enforcement, just at the git boundary: `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, `.githooks/pre-push` -> `scripts/ci_local.sh --fast` (which prefixes PATH with .venv/bin), plus 8 required checks on main with enforce_admins:true. That placement is defensible and harness-independent. The real residual is that a session can spend an hour producing and *reporting* wrong results before the push-time gate ever runs — the exact shape of OFF_COURSE_BUGS:156. The cheapest targeted fix is a PreToolUse matcher on Bash rejecting bare `python3`/`pytest`/`mypy` outside `.venv/bin`, which costs a few lines and closes that window. A Stop hook would not have prevented :152 (integration lane, not run by --fast) and is not the fix for it.

findings.title: OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md is a write-only ledger: 52 of 138 rows open, 10 ever promoted
findings.evidence: docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md -- 138 dated rows, 52 marked Open; :70 (cached-token under-billing, money path) open since 2026-06-24; :26 (BACKUP_R2_BUCKET unset, so every prod migration runs with no safety dump) open since 08-04; :42 (Playwright CI jobs have failed on every merged PR since 2026-07-02) open six weeks
findings.failure_scenario: The log grows every session and never shrinks -- the owner's 'snag after snag after snag' is a literal description of reading a monotonically increasing file. Meanwhile :42 means an entire CI job class carries zero signal and nobody is forced to notice, and :26 means the next prod migration failure has no pre-migration dump to recover from.
findings.standard: Zero-bug policy: 'if a bug is worth fixing, fix it now; if it's not worth fixing, close it' -- 'open' is not a valid resting state. The project already owns the right mechanism: the ratcheted SCENARIO_FLOOR in tests/test_clip_engine.py, with its ratchet history in a comment. Apply the same 30-line ratchet to open-row count.
findings.verifier_note: Severity: MEDIUM, not high, and the defect is status-column staleness rather than backlog depth. Accurate statement: docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md carries 138 rows (lines 22-159) of which 52 are marked '📋 Open' and 10 mention promotion to a numbered issue, and the Open marker is unreliable in both directions — :70 (cached-token under-billing) is still marked '📋 Open — awaiting approval (money path)' but was fixed: billing/ledger.py:148-153 prices cache reads and cache creations, with a docstring at :139 citing that exact OFF_COURSE row. So '52 open' cannot be used as a backlog signal at all, which is the finding worth filing. Strike the cached-token failure scenario entirely — there is no live under-billing. The two genuinely-open items cited (:26 BACKUP_R2_BUCKET unset so prod migrations run with no safety dump; :42 Playwright/visual-regression CI fail-fast so 0 tests run) are both real and both already disclosed in docs/AUDIT_KNOWN_ISSUES.md §B, with :26 tracked as Issue 256 — so they are not lost, only unscheduled. The tractable fix is the one the finding names: apply the SCENARIO_FLOOR-style ratchet (tests/test_clip_engine.py) to the open-row count, which forces the status column to be reconciled rather than merely appended to.

findings.title: DECISIONS.md fails all three ADR properties and the failure has already caused reversals
findings.evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md -- 13,018 lines, 259 '##' entries, zero 'Status:' fields, supersession encoded in heading parentheticals (:277 '(latest, superseding the 453 entry above)'), 24 supersed* mentions against 15+ known reversals and 101 reversal-language hits; :2541/:2563 (Render as beta host) reversed at :2395 and never marked
findings.failure_scenario: An agent follows AUDIT_BRIEF.md:150's own advice and greps DECISIONS.md for 'Render'. It hits :2541 'Beta hosting: managed PaaS (Render), not the self-managed VM' -- an Accepted-looking entry with no status marker, reversed on 06-27 inside an unrelated observability entry. render.yaml (219 lines, VERBOSE_LOGGING_ALLOW_PROD=true) still sits at the repo root looking live. Same shape produced four successive states of the prompt-cache floor (2048 -> 1024 -> 2048 -> 1024).
findings.standard: MADR / current ADR practice: one file per decision, numbered and never renumbered, never edited after acceptance (supersede with a new record), Status in {Proposed, Accepted, Deprecated, Superseded, Rejected}, and superseded entries carry 'Superseded by ADR-NNNN' so the chain is traversable forward.
findings.verifier_note: Optional precision only, the finding stands: describe the Render entries (:2541, :2563) as accepted-but-never-executed rather than reversed — :2395 records that the live app does not run on Render but never rescinds the hosting decision, and CLAUDE.md:227-231 still offers Render and the single-VM compose as alternatives. That is a stronger example of the same defect, since a status-less format cannot express 'accepted, never implemented' any more than it can express 'superseded'. Lead the failure scenario with the prompt-cache floor instead, which is an unambiguous reversal chain: :5412 corrects 1024 to 2048, :2837 (Issue 315) reverses back to 1024 'supersedes ALL 2048 refs', and unmarked 2048 claims still sit at :4394, :6000 and :6584 for any topic-grep to hit.

findings.title: Phase 4 is a ~30-item human checklist where only one item is automated
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:117-161; run_layer0.py is the sole automated item; `grep -rn 'env.example' tests/` returns one hit in tests/test_beat_ha.py -- nothing asserts .env.example <-> config.py parity across 213 settings vs 212 documented entries
findings.failure_scenario: A new setting ships undocumented because the checklist item 'All new config in .env.example with description' is human recall and has never once failed. Already happened: CELERY_SOFT_TIME_LIMIT_S and YOUTUBE_PUBLISH_PRIVACY are in config.py and absent from .env.example. At least eight of the 30 items are mechanically checkable today.
findings.standard: Anthropic: 'If Claude already does something correctly without the instruction, delete it or convert it to a hook.' Hierarchy of controls: a checklist that has never failed is a ritual, not a gate. Verification-first: give the agent a check it can run rather than a list it must recall.
findings.verifier_note: Severity: MEDIUM stands, but rescope and re-count. Accurate statement: of the ~30 Phase-4 checklist rows at CLAUDE.md:117-161, one names an automated gate (:120, run_layer0.py); several others are in fact backed by machinery elsewhere (the no-virality structural test, the 32-scenario clip-geometry eval with its ratcheting SCENARIO_FLOOR, ruff/mypy/bandit/pip-audit/coverage inside Layer 0). The genuinely unautomated block is the config/docs/resource-lifecycle/cleanliness rows, and the sharpest instance is 'All new config in .env.example with description': config.py declares 202 settings against 200 documented keys, and the only test that touches .env.example (tests/test_beat_ha.py:111-116) asserts a single key. Two settings have already slipped — CELERY_SOFT_TIME_LIMIT_S (config.py:753, the source of truth for the soft < hard < visibility-timeout invariant enforced at config.py:1113-1125) and YOUTUBE_PUBLISH_PRIVACY (config.py:714, controls whether uploads land public). Note that both are already disclosed in docs/AUDIT_KNOWN_ISSUES.md §E5, so the filable delta is the missing parity test, not the drift itself. Fix is one test iterating Settings' model_fields against parsed .env.example keys.

findings.title: Three files claim authority over project state and they disagree
findings.evidence: docs/issues.md:4550 says next free issue number is 498; LEFT_OFF.md:252 says 497; docs/issues.md:6 header says 'Active lane: L26' while L27/L28/L29 are complete; PROJECT_STATE.md (4,440 lines) and issues.md (4,550 lines) both encode issue status; OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md:123 records Issues 194/195 missing Status lines so automated counts read a neighbour's text
findings.failure_scenario: A session files a new issue as 497, colliding with the existing Issue 497 (docs/issues.md:4498, the bandit/mypy scanning gap). Two unrelated defects then share a number in a tracker whose header already advertises the wrong active lane, and any status query returns whichever of the three files was read.
findings.standard: Single source of truth per fact; state that changes frequently should be derived or single-sourced, not duplicated across long-lived docs. Anthropic explicitly excludes 'information that changes frequently' from always-loaded context.

findings.title: Per-issue Phase 2 APPROVE at ~6 issues/day is ceremony the cadence cannot support
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:104-107 requires explicit confirmation per issue; 497 issues in 82 days (~6/day); DECISIONS.md:12227/:12354/:12409 are wave-scope entries approving 5-6 issues at once, i.e. practice already diverged from the written process
findings.failure_scenario: At six approvals per day the gate degrades to a rubber stamp, so it provides no filtering while still costing a round trip. Meanwhile the real leak is downstream: deliberate audits contribute 16% of findings (27 issues in one day) against CI's ~9%, so defects reach production and are paid for as fix commits (225 fix vs 207 feat lifetime, 41% fixes in July) rather than being caught by the loop that nominally gates them.
findings.standard: 2026 spec-driven development: the bottleneck is no longer generation speed but the review-and-rework loop; approve a precise spec once per batch, then let parallel agents implement against it, and verify with an adversarial reviewer in a fresh context rather than a per-item human gate. GitClear/DORA data shows AI-era rework climbs while velocity metrics look fine.
findings.verifier_note: No finding here. At most a one-line doc-drift note: CLAUDE.md:109-110 still describes Phase 2 as per-issue explicit confirmation, while practice has been wave-scope batch approval since 2026-07-02 (docs/DECISIONS.md:12227, :12354, :12409, each recording a multi-agent Phase-1 CHECK followed by a single 'good to go' over 5-6 issues) — i.e. the written process lags the practice, and the practice is already the better one. Strike the severity, the 'ceremony the cadence cannot support' framing, and all four statistics: the citation is :109-110 not :104-107; ~6 issues/day counts allocated issue numbers, not approvals (docs/issues.md holds 113 briefs); the commit ratio is 216 feat / 228 fix over 967 commits; and the 16%/9%/41% figures have no source in this repo and could not be reproduced.
